Wider Sports News.body:
Genius Sports, a global leader in sports data and technology, and NBA All-Star and entrepreneur Chris Paul have announced the launch of a new athlete-led sports media company created in partnership with Paul’s Ohh Dip!!! Entertainment and Connor Schell’s Words + Pictures.

The new company will develop original sports programming and content franchises built around the perspectives of athletes and creators, combining their access and expertise with Genius Sports’ official data, AI and technology. Wider Sports News.title: NFL commissioner Goodell says league could restructure media deals to attract streamers
Wider Sports News.summary: American football league believes streaming services can improve accessibility and drive revenue growth despite possible political opposition. The post NFL commissioner Goodell says league could restructure media deals to attract streamers appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The National League Football (NFL) could restructure its media packages to reflect the rise of streaming platforms when it next goes to market. Commissioner Roger Goodell told CNBC that the league was considering adjusting its approach to reflect changing consumption habits in order to maximise both revenues and accessibility but would not be drawn on whether any changes would come into effect for the next cycle.

“One of the things we’re doing as a league is talking to our partners, talking to future partners, potential partners … and evaluating, should we repackage our current packages? Should we think differently about where we go with those things?” Goodell is quoted as saying.

Wider Sports News.title: World Rugby confirms qualification pathway for Los Angeles 2028 Olympics Games
Wider Sports News.summary: World Rugby confirms qualification pathway for Los Angeles 2028 Olympics Games Asia Rugby
Wider Sports News.body:
World Rugby has confirmed the qualification pathway for rugby sevens at the LA28 Olympic Games, with 12 men’s and 12 women’s teams set to compete for Olympic glory. A total of 24 teams will compete at LA28, with each qualified National Olympic Committee (NOC) able to select a delegation of 12 players per team.

As hosts, USA will receive an automatic quota place in both the men’s and women’s competitions. The race for Olympic qualification will begin during the HSBC SVNS 2027 season, which is set to kick-off in Dubai in November 2026 before concluding in Bordeaux at the end of May 2027.

Wider Sports News.title: Benfica invests in education with creation of Benfica Institute for Sport Excellence
Wider Sports News.summary: Knowledge-sharing hub unveiled, with first course already underway, to underline the club's commitment to sporting excellence The post Benfica invests in education with creation of Benfica Institute for Sport Excellence appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Lisbon, September 8th, 2026 — Sport Lisboa e Benfica officially launched the Benfica Institute for Sport Excellence, a living knowledge-sharing hub that reflects a significant investment by the club in education and the sharing of its world renowned methodology and elite expertise with the wider sporting world, spanning talent development, applied research, innovation and specialist training for the football and sports industry.

The Institute will operate as an open platform for education, research and innovation aimed primarily at professionals and students seeking to work in sports, comprising six courses taught in Portuguese and English. Teaching staff are drawn largely from Benfica’s own football and sporting structure, alongside international university lecturers and sports scientists. Courses combine online and in-person formats, with in-person sessions held at Benfica Campus and Estádio da Luz.

Wider Sports News.title: Formula 1 has won the battle for attention. Now it needs to win the battle for loyalty.
Wider Sports News.summary: F1 has mastered the art of attracting a new generation of fans — but turning that surge in attention into lasting loyalty will be the defining challenge for teams, sponsors and the sport itself. The post Formula 1 has won the battle for attention. Now it needs to win the battle for loyalty. appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Bernie Ecclestone once dismissed social media as “nonsense”. He said he would rather chase the 70-year-old with money to spend than worry about building a younger audience online. It feels slightly mad now, given what Formula 1 has become.

When Liberty Media took over in 2017, the sport had a problem. TV audiences had been heading in the wrong direction and there was very little sense of where the next generation of fans would come from. The racing was still there, but F1 had spent years making itself strangely difficult to get close to.

The post A US$9.6bn sale, stalled TV renewals and flags on the play: The business of the NFL in 2026 appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The National Football League (NFL) is back and, as ever, bigger and bolder than before. A new season for the world’s richest sports league gets underway with a Super Bowl rematch between the New England Patriots and champions Seattle Seahawks – now confirmed as the most expensive franchise in NFL history.

An extended opening week continues on Thursday evening – technically Friday morning in Australia – as the giant Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) hosts the Los Angeles Rams and the San Francisco 49ers. That event will be shown worldwide as part of an expanded agreement with streaming giant Netflix; Paris and Rio de Janeiro will join Melbourne as International Series circuit debutants in the autumn.

Wider Sports News.title: World Rugby confirms LA28 Sevens Qualification Path

Wider Sports News.body:
World Rugby has confirmed the qualification pathway for rugby sevens at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games, with 12 men’s and 12 women’s teams set to compete. Host nation USA will receive automatic places in both competitions.

The qualification race will begin during the HSBC SVNS 2027 season, starting in Dubai in November 2026 and concluding in Bordeaux at the end of May 2027. The four highest-ranked eligible men’s teams and four highest-ranked eligible women’s teams in the final World Championship standings, excluding hosts USA, will qualify directly for LA28.

Wider Sports News.title: Consortium led by L Catterton in partnership with HYROX founders acquires Infront’s majority stake in HYROX
Wider Sports News.summary: HYROX’s rapid rise from emerging fitness format to global mass-participation phenomenon has opened the door to its next phase of growth, with ambitions spanning millions more participants, new products and a potential Olympic future. The post Consortium led by L Catterton in partnership with HYROX founders acquires Infront’s majority stake in HYROX appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
LONDON / ZUG, September 8th, 2026 – Infront Sports & Media AG (Infront), the leading international sports business company, today announced the completion of the sale of its majority stake in HYROX to a consortium led by L Catterton, the largest global consumer-focused investment firm, alongside HYROX founders Christian Toetzke and Moritz Fürste. WndrCo, the investment firm founded and led by Jeffrey Katzenburg and his partner Sujay Jaswa, will also participate in the transaction. This marks an important milestone in HYROX’s continued growth. Financial terms were not disclosed.

HYROX was created by Christian Toetzke, an industry veteran in the international cycling and triathlon world, and Moritz Fürste, one of Germany’s greatest ever field hockey players and successful entrepreneur. In less than a decade HYROX has become a global phenomenon including events, training programmes and affiliate gyms around the world that together deliver a competition format that inspires and unites athletes. The new partnership brings together HYROX’s category-defining brand and community with L Catterton’s extensive experience scaling high-growth consumer and fitness businesses around the world. Together, the founders and L Catterton will continue to invest in delivering an exceptional experience for HYROX athletes and the development of Hybrid Racing as a global sport.

Wider Sports News.title: “I sold at the lowest”: Andrea Radrizzani on his Leeds mistake, DAZN exit timeline and where he’s investing next
Wider Sports News.summary: Armed with experiences at MP & Silva, Leeds United and Aser Ventures, Andrea Radrizzani tells SportsPro where the real value now lies for investors. The post “I sold at the lowest”: Andrea Radrizzani on his Leeds mistake, DAZN exit timeline and where he’s investing next appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Leeds United’s fanbase has a reputation for being one of the most loyal in English soccer. Andrea Radrizzani learned that quickly when he bought the club for UK£45 million (US$61 million) in 2017. The Italian was already well known within sports industry circles as the co-founder of MP & Silva, the now-defunct international media rights agency he established in 2004 before selling his shares in 2016, when the company had reached a US$1 billion valuation. Leeds, however, represented his first move into soccer club ownership.

Some investors might have preferred to cut their teeth at a smaller club before taking over one of the best-followed teams in England. However, after hearing Liverpool great Kenny Dalglish refer to Leeds as a sleeping giant, the opportunity to bring success back to one of soccer’s true one-club cities proved too good to turn down for Radrizzani, who has described himself as an underdog in business.

Rugby.title: Two-time World Cup winner targets 'unbelievable' career first
Rugby.summary: Natasha ‘Mo’ Hunt has packed plenty into an illustrious career already.
Rugby.body:
Natasha ‘Mo’ Hunt has packed plenty into an illustrious career already. The 37-year-old has earned 89 England caps to date, lifted multiple Guinness Women’s Six Nations titles, become a two-time Olympian by competing at the 2016 Rio Olympics and delayed Tokyo Olympics, and played big part in her club Gloucester Hartpury’s remarkable Premiership Women’s Rugby ‘three-peat’ success between 2022-2025.

Those achievements only scratch the surface of the renowned Red Roses scrum-half’s decorated career. Now, however, Hunt has her sights set on a new challenge – becoming part of history with the inaugural British & Irish Lions Women’s tour to New Zealand in 2027.

Rugby.body:
Japan are through to the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup 2026 Final after defeating the USA 63-14 at Osaka’s Hanazono Rugby Stadium on Saturday. The Brave Blossoms will play for the title in front of a home crowd in Tokyo, where they will face defending champions Fiji.

There were some similarities in how the semi-finals played out, with both Fiji and Japan racing out to early leads before their North American opponents fought back. Fiji led 45-17 with less than 20 minutes left, but the Canadians hit back with two late tries.

Rugby.title: Donnell eyes Irish call-up after Ulster move
Rugby.summary: New Ulster signing Ben Donnell says a motivating factor in his move to the province was the chance to force his way into the Ireland set-up and play international rugby.
Rugby.body:
New Ulster signing Ben Donnell said a motivating factor in his move to the province was the chance to force his way into the Ireland set-up and play international rugby. The 26-year-old is Irish-qualified through his Belfast-born father and as well as the chance to discover where his father grew up, he is aiming to catch Ireland head coach Andy Farrell's eye at his new club.

"My dad being from here, I wanted to see what Belfast was like and what it was like for him growing up here, but also I'm Irish-qualified and it gives me the chance to play international rugby," he told BBC Sport NI's Nicola McCarthy.

Rugby.title: Fiji through to another PNC decider after powering past Canada in Osaka
Rugby.summary: Fiji are one win away from another Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup title after beating Canada in an electric semi-final.
Rugby.body:
Fiji are one win away from another Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup title after beating Canada 45-29 in an electric semi-final. It was the first part of a double-header at Osaka’s Hanazono Rugby Stadium on Saturday, with PNC hosts Japan taking on the USA in the other match.

The Flying Fijians took out the PNC crown the last time the event was held in Japan two years ago, before successfully going back-to-back. Joji Nasova starred as Fiji claimed more silverware with a six-point win over Japan on September 21, 2025.

Rugby.title: Canada veteran on impact of team’s 2019 RWC typhoon clean-up efforts
Rugby.summary: But the opportunity to chase history in that Test never came, with an extremely powerful tropical cyclone making landfall.
Rugby.body:
Canada hadn’t won a Men’s Rugby World Cup match in more than eight years when the side walked off the field on October 8, 2019, following a 66-7 defeat to eventual champions the Springboks in Kobe.

The Canadians had also suffered defeats to Six Nations side Italy and the then two-time reigning world champion All Blacks, but they had one more match scheduled in a brutal pool of death – a clash with Namibia they had been targeting.

Rugby.title: Hunt sets sights on Lions tour after injury return
Rugby.summary: England scrum-half Natasha Hunt says the inaugural British and Irish Lions women's tour to New Zealand - the first Test of which is exactly a year away today - is a massive motivation as she prepares to make her comeback from injury.
Rugby.body:
England scrum-half Natasha Hunt says the inaugural British and Irish Lions women's tour to New Zealand - the first Test of which is exactly a year away - is a massive motivation as she prepares to make her comeback from injury.

The 37-year-old sustained knee ligament damage during England's Six Nations opener against Ireland in April. She was sidelined for the rest of the Red Roses' Grand-Slam winning campaign and Gloucester-Hartpury's run to the PWR semi-finals, but starts at nine in England's WXV Global Series opener against Australia in Salford on Saturday.

Rugby.title: Charity Williams: The Test debutant with 10 years of international experience and two Olympic medals
Rugby.summary: Not so long ago, Charity Williams did not know what new experiences her rugby career could offer.
Rugby.body:
Not so long ago, Charity Williams did not know what new experiences her rugby career could offer. At 29, the Canadian has represented her country in rugby sevens at three Olympic Games. She has the silver and bronze medals to prove it.

This weekend, Williams will make her Test rugby debut for Canada as a starter against Scotland in their WXV Global Series opener. It is not often a player makes their Test debut with 11 years of international rugby experience already in the bank. The Toronto-born wing is one of three North American debutants, with her sevens teammate Savannah Bauder and prop forward Sophie McDonald in line for their first caps from the replacements.

Rugby.title: ‘It hurt my soul’: Rachel Malcolm hopes Test return can reignite Scotland’s defensive grit
Rugby.summary: Talismanic captain Rachel Malcolm believes that Scotland lost their identity as a team between late last year and during the Guinness Women’s Six Nations in 2026.
Rugby.body:
Talismanic captain Rachel Malcolm believes that Scotland lost their identity as a team between late last year and during the Guinness Women’s Six Nations in 2026. She has also stated that shipping 267 points – including 41 tries – in five games as they finished a disappointing fifth in that Women’s Six Nations campaign “hurt” her soul given the importance the squad has placed on defence in recent years.

Now, with a busy period of WXV Global Series action getting underway this weekend, the 35-year-old Trailfinders Women’s back-row has vowed to help get the national team back up to the levels that they know they are capable of.

Rugby.title: 'It's been tough for Beauden': Dave Rennie explains All Blacks' No.10 switch
Rugby.summary: Dave Rennie has shed light on the All Blacks' No.10 selection plan for the Greatest Rivalry tour after announcing a change at the position for the first time this year.
Rugby.body:
Dave Rennie has shed light on the All Blacks‘ No.10 selection plan for the Greatest Rivalry tour after announcing a change at the position for the first time this year. The coach has turned to experience for the series decider in Baltimore, dropping Ruben Love in favour of Richie Mo’unga and bringing Beauden Barrett onto the bench.

Mo’unga served as All Blacks game-driver in a hotly contested midweek game against the Lions in Johannesburg three weeks ago, in what were his first minutes in the black jersey since the 2023 Rugby World Cup final, albeit a non-Test match. Having reclaimed his New Zealand eligibility after three years in Japan, the 32-year-old will now don the famous black No.10 shirt in the international arena for the first time in 1050 days.

Rugby.summary: Sean Lynn's Wales have suffered a triple injury blow ahead of their WXV Global Series campaign starting.
Rugby.body:
Sean Lynn’s Wales have suffered a triple injury blow ahead of their WXV Global Series campaign starting. One week before they take on South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park, 42-cap prop Donna Rose [ankle], as well as Kelsie Webster [hand] and Hanna Tudor [foot] have all been ruled out of their four fixtures.

In the coming weeks, Wales will also play the USA Women’s Eagles prior to a two-match tour of Japan. The 13th-ranked team in the world are aiming to end their one-year spell without a win, which dates back to July 2025.

Rugby.title: Finn Russell on his future: I won't make the same mistakes as the past
Rugby.summary: The mercurial fly-half has a couple of seasons left on his £1 million-year contract at Bath and will be 35 by the time the 2027 World Cup in Australia is over.
Rugby.body:
Scotland and Lions star Finn Russell doesn’t want to repeat the mistakes of the past and set parameters around the length of his Test career. The mercurial fly-half has a couple of seasons left on his £1 million-year contract at Bath and will be 35 by the time the 2027 World Cup in Australia is over.

By then, Russell will have certainly become a caps centurion for Scotland – he is five short of the milestone at present – and could have even overtaken Ross Ford (110 caps) as his country’s record holder for most Test appearances.

Rugby.summary: This weekend the WXV Global Series and WXV Global Series Challenger will get underway and bringing 18 leading women's international teams into action.
Rugby.body:
This weekend, the WXV Global Series and WXV Global Series Challenger will get underway, bringing 18 leading women’s international teams into action. The WXV Global Series sees the world’s top 12 ranked teams – Australia, Canada, England, France, Italy, Ireland, Japan, New Zealand, Scotland, South Africa, USA and Wales – play each other in a home-and-away cross-regional touring model in an eight-week global window.

The first WXV Global Series Challenger event takes place at Kai Tak Sports Park, where Fiji, Hong Kong China, Netherlands, Samoa, Spain and Brazil will play three matches each.

Rugby.title: 'I'm here to compete': Meet Zimbabwe's box-office 'Transporter' who Harlequins signed via Instagram
Rugby.summary: Edward Sigauke is an exhilarating talent, plucked from left field on social media, and determined to seize his golden ticket to the Prem.
Rugby.body:
When Ed Spokes, the Harlequins head of recruitment, slid into Edward Sigauke’s DMs, the Zimbabwean hot rod thought the message might be a prank. He was midway through a Nations Cup campaign which took his international record to nine tries in 11 Tests, and burnished his credentials as one of the game’s most spectacular raw talents, but the idea of attracting Gallagher Prem interest still felt fanciful.

Two months later, the 22-year-old wing sits in a Guildford apartment; Quins kitbag in the corner of his room, play sheet on his laptop, and head somewhat spinning after a sense-scrambling move to Southwest London.

Rugby.title: Will Stuart to make playing comeback nine months after horror injury
Rugby.summary: Stuart went off early in the second half of Bath's Champions Cup victory against Munster in mid-December last year and missed the remainder of the 2025/26 season.
Rugby.body:
England prop Will Stuart will play his first game since rupturing his Achilles tendon when Bath take on Bedford tonight in a pre-season friendly at Goldington Road, which is being streamed by online broadcaster Clubber TV.

Stuart went off early in the second half of Bath’s Champions Cup victory against Munster in mid-December last year and missed the remainder of the 2025/26 season. But the tight-head, who committed his future to Bath in February by signing a new contract through to 2028, is now ready to return after a long period of rehabilitation and has been named on the bench.

Rugby.title: Meet the motivator, enforcer and observer who form the Red Roses leadership group
Rugby.summary: Sitting around a table outside England’s hotel, the trio of captain Meg Jones and vice-captains Amy Cokayne and Alex Matthews are describing their individual leadership styles.
Rugby.body:
Sitting around a table outside England’s hotel, the trio of captain Meg Jones and vice-captains Amy Cokayne and Alex Matthews are describing their individual leadership styles.

Jones, to surely no one’s surprise, is the motivator, eager to encourage her team-mates on and off the field when she can, leading with “a lot of passion and pride”. Cokayne has a slightly different approach. “I’ll probably say the discipliner or the enforcer,” explaining that if a message needs to be sent, it will most likely come from her. “I’m quite a direct human,” she adds, which checks out given Cokayne’s background in the RAF.

Rugby.title: All Blacks coaching legend Steve Hansen makes dramatic code switch
Rugby.summary: Aussie NRL outfit Manly Sea Eagles have appointed World Cup-winning coach Steve Hansen as their football performance director.
Rugby.body:
Australian National Rugby League (NRL) outfit Manly Sea Eagles have appointed World Cup-winning coach Steve Hansen as their football performance director. Hansen will work closely with Sea Eagles head coach Kieran Foran, CEO Jason King, and the club’s football department, as they look to utilise the former All Blacks boss’ experience in creating a winning culture after a disappointing season.

Manly finished ninth on the 17-team NRL ladder. “To have someone of Steve Hansen’s experience, knowledge and proven record of building winning cultures joining our football department is a massive opportunity for this club,” Foran said.

Rugby.title: No plans for Ireland Six Nations game in US
Rugby.summary: There are "currently no plans or discussions" relating to Ireland playing a Six Nations match in the United States, the Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) says.
Rugby.body:
There are "currently no plans or discussions" relating to Ireland playing a Six Nations match in the United States, the Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) says. World Rugby's chief executive Alan Gilpin said on Wednesday that it would help any nation that wants to switch a Six Nations match to the US, as it continues its drive to spread the game stateside.

He used the example of Ireland v Italy as a game that would resonate with expatriate fans in the United States and could help the sport further establish itself there. But, in a statement issued on Friday, the IRFU dismissed the idea that it was considering moving any fixtures to the US.

Rugby.title: Springbok Women unveil WXV squad as 'wider plan' revealed
Rugby.summary: Springbok Women co-coaches Franzel September and Laurian Johannes-Haupt have named the squad the European leg of their WXV Global Series campaign.
Rugby.body:
Springbok Women co-coaches Franzel September and Laurian Johannes-Haupt have named the squad the European leg of their WXV Global Series campaign. In the coming weeks, South Africa will play Tests against Wales, Italy and Spain, prior to return to Cape Town for back-to-back matches against Ireland.

Already in 2026 the team have retained their Rugby Africa Women’s Cup title, played two-Test series against the USA Women’s Eagles and Fiji, and lost 52-20 to the Black Ferns at FNB Stadium. Out of the eight matches the team have played this calendar year, they have won six.

Rugby.title: Prop Vunipola set to retire before Leicester move
Rugby.summary: Former England prop Mako Vunipola was planning to retire as a player before a phone call from from Leicester Tigers head coach Geoff Parling changed his mind.
Rugby.body:
Former England prop Mako Vunipola says he was planning to retire before a phone call from from Leicester Tigers head coach Geoff Parling changed his mind. The 35-year-old ex-Saracens front-rower, who won four Premiership titles and and the European Champions Cup three times with the London club, has moved back to England's top flight after two years in France with Vannes to play under former international team-mate Parling.

The pair featured for England together more than a decade ago and were also part of the British and Irish Lions team that toured Australia in 2013. Vunipola said it was "pretty random" how he was convinced to make a U-turn on his decision to hang up his boots and join a Leicester side that Parling guided to the Prem semi-finals in his first season at the helm.

Rugby.title: Harlequins homecoming for international PREM winner James Lang
Rugby.summary: Lang's signing completes Harlequins' squad for the 2026/27 season, with the former RGC 1404 player facing stiff competition in the centres from the likes of Oscar Beard, Luke Northmore, Bryn Bradley, Sean Kerr and Ben Waghorn.
Rugby.body:
Centre James Lang has returned to Harlequins for the second time in his career after being released by Edinburgh. Lang, 31, has spent the past five years North of the Border, clocking up 90 appearances for the capital club.

A serious ankle injury in the Champions Cup round of 16 defeat to Leinster cut short his involvement last season and proved to be his final game for the club. A product of the Harlequins academy, Lang had a spell playing in North Wales before returning to London, where he enjoyed a five-season stint in the quarters.

Rugby.title: Ireland's Reilly hoping to put injury woes behind her
Rugby.summary: Ireland scrum-half Aoibheann Reilly says she is "grateful" to be back among the squad after recovering from her latest injury setback.
Rugby.body:
Ireland scrum-half Aoibheann Reilly says she is "grateful" to be back in Scott Bemand's squad as she aims to put her injury woes behind her and play a significant part in the forthcoming WXV series.

The Irish number nine missed this year's Women's Six Nations tournament after breaking her fibula and has also battled back from ACL injuries to her left and right legs which she suffered in the space of nine months.

Rugby.title: Rugby's Greatest Rivalry finale will decide World Rankings supremacy
Rugby.summary: New Zealand's victory in the first Test at Ellis Park ended the Springboks' 11-month reign at the top of the rankings, but they were only able to hold onto that position for a week.
Rugby.body:
The number one spot in the World Rugby Men’s Rankings could change hands for the third time since the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series began in August. If the All Blacks win this week’s concluding Test in Baltimore and level the series at 2-2, they will once again be rated as the best team in the world, a status that most Springboks would dispute, given they have won back-to-back Rugby World Cups.

New Zealand’s victory in the first Test at Ellis Park ended the Springboks’ 11-month reign at the top of the rankings, but they were only able to hold onto that position for a week after being beaten in the second Test in Cape Town.

Rugby.title: Teams, form and storylines: Pacific Nations Cup semi-final guide
Rugby.summary: The Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup 2026 semi-finals are taking place this weekend as part of a double-header at Osaka’s Hanazono Rugby Stadium.
Rugby.body:
The Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup 2026 semi-finals are taking place this weekend as part of a double-header at Osaka’s Hanazono Rugby Stadium. Fiji are looking to defend their PNC title, while Japan, the USA and Canada look to dethrone the reigning champions.

It’s a bit of a preview for some key Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 pool-stage clashes too, with the semi-final matchups set to be repeated at that tournament. Japan and the USA Eagles will face off on Saturday evening, and meet again less than 400 days later.

Rugby.title: One year until first women's Lions Test
Rugby.summary: With the first British and Irish Lions women's Test 12 months away, BBC Sport looks at how preparations are going and whether the tour will be a success.
Rugby.body:
Sporting history will be made one year from today when the first British and Irish Lions women's team runs out at Auckland's Go Media Stadium. They will be taking on six-time world champions New Zealand on 11 September 2027 in the first of a three-Test series.

Lions chief executive Ben Calveley says the month-long tour, which was announced in 2024, will be a "hugely significant" milestone and "something truly special for the women's game".

Rugby.title: The Canada centre who experienced a Test debut week twice
Rugby.summary: Ince continued to reach even higher heights after being named to potentially debut in Canada’s Nations Cup opener against Spain.
Rugby.body:
Jacob Ince led the way as the Guelph Gryphons claimed a first-ever men’s national championship last November, and the midfielder was rewarded with a place in Canada’s squad for the all-new World Rugby Nations Cup in July.

“I had never actually played a professional game,” Ince said, having been given the chance to rub shoulders with Test veterans like Lucas Rumball and Ben LeSage. The 23-year-old then had the fairly rare experience of going through a debut Test week twice.

Rugby.summary: Super Round will return to Christchurch’s One NZ Stadium next season, with Super Rugby Pacific unveiling the five-match schedule on Friday.
Rugby.body:
Super Round will return to Christchurch’s One NZ Stadium next season, with Super Rugby Pacific unveiling the five-match schedule on Friday. It’s an announcement that follows the success of the 2026 edition, with 10 Super Rugby Pacific teams taking the field across three days.

Thousands of fans packed out the state-of-the-art venue for Super Round last season, with the Crusaders defeating the NSW Waratahs first up. The hosts will again feature in the opening match, when the three-day event gets underway on April 2.

Rugby.title: All Blacks concede latest injuries have left leadership hole ahead of decider
Rugby.summary: Codie Taylor will step back into the captaincy role against the Springboks at M&T Bank Stadium with a historic tour result on the line, after sitting out the third Test.
Rugby.body:
When All Blacks captain Ardie Savea left the field injured on Saturday at FNB Stadium, Luke Jacobson took over the captaincy duties only to also suffer a tour-ending injury. Also losing Quinn Tupaea in the Test left New Zealand with a significant hole in their leadership group heading into the decisive final Test in Baltimore.

It’s a leadership deficit that both supersub Wallace Sititi and head coach Dave Rennie have conceded will hurt the team, which faces a 2-1 series deficit after consecutive losses in Cape Town and Soweto.

Rugby.title: England captain Jones calls for fertility support
Rugby.summary: England captain Meg Jones wants the Red Roses to have access to fertility support and egg freezing.
Rugby.body:
Meg Jones, captain of the England women's rugby union team, wants Red Roses players to have access to fertility support and egg freezing. Speaking to BBC Sport, Jones said: "Why should my opportunity to have a family be taken away from me because I want to pursue my career?"

Jones revealed she has already started her fertility journey with her fiancee after visiting a clinic to have their egg count checked. The 29-year-old says that she's an "open book" on some subjects and wants to "share her journey" as she discusses both her upcoming wedding and family planning with equal comfort.

Rugby.title: Ireland joining elite only a matter of time
Rugby.summary: Aoife Wafer says Ireland are capable of joining the world's elite teams as they build on progress made in recent years.
Rugby.body:
Back row Aoife Wafer has predicted it is "only a matter of time" before Ireland join the ranks of the very best teams in the world. The number eight was speaking as the Irish squad prepare for a WXV campaign in which they will face the United States in Dublin on 20 September, and then Japan twice on home soil, before travelling for two Tests with South Africa in late October.

Ireland were narrowly edged out by France at the quarter-final stage of last year's World Cup and have finished third behind England and the French in the past two Women's Six Nations championships.

Rugby.title: How Scotland are 'striving for excellence' at WXV after challenging 2026
Rugby.summary: Scotland fly-half Helen Nelson says the team are striving for excellence in the WXV Global Series as they look to bounce back from a difficult start to 2026.
Rugby.body:
Scotland fly-half Helen Nelson says the team are striving for excellence in the WXV Global Series as they look to bounce back from a difficult start to 2026. The team finished fifth in the Guinness Women’s Six Nations, which included heavy defeats against teams such as England and Ireland.

They have then dealt with the departure of their head coach Sione Fukofuka, who confirmed he had left the set up last month. Dave Butcher is taking interim charge of Scotland for their matches over the next two months against Canada, New Zealand and Australia. Nelson added the vibes in camp are good and the standards have been set high.

Rugby.title: Pat Lam provides positive Ellis Genge report despite missing England camp
Rugby.summary: Bristol Bears coach Pat Lam has revealed that loosehead Ellis Genge wasn’t involved in England’s 36-man three-day camp this week after being given extra time after his summer toil in the Nations Championship.
Rugby.body:
Bristol Bears coach Pat Lam has revealed that loosehead Ellis Genge wasn’t involved in England’s 36-man three-day camp this week after being given extra time after his summer toil in the Nations Championship.

The England vice-captain played all 12 of their tests last season, and Lam says that he was given an extra week off to recover from his massive workload. And he says that Genge is “looking fresh” and that he fully supports the decision that was made by Red Rose boss Steve Borthwick earlier in the summer.

Rugby.title: France draft trio of sevens stars for WXV opener against ‘fantastic’ Black Ferns
Rugby.summary: François Ratier has called on the France Sevens squad ahead of his team's WXV Global Series opener against the Black Ferns on Sunday.
Rugby.body:
François Ratier has called on the France Sevens squad ahead of his team’s WXV Global Series opener against the Black Ferns on Sunday. Both Chloé Jacquet and Kelly Arbey have won Test caps before, while Lili Dezou will make her international debut at outside centre. She partners Teani Feleu in midfield.

Dezou, 22, plays her club rugby for Stade Toulousain and represented her country at their home Olympic Games in 2024. Upon announcing his squad, Ratier confirmed that the trio would only play in France’s opening WXV Global Series fixture before returning to sevens camp.

Rugby.title: 'Things can change quickly'
Rugby.summary: Fraser Dingwall says his omission from England's past two squads is "disappointing", but does not make a return impossible.
Rugby.body:
Fraser Dingwall said his omission from England's past two squads had felt "disappointing", but did not mean the door was closed for a return. The 27-year-old Northampton Saints club captain was England's first-choice inside centre in a successful autumn that included victory over New Zealand. He also started for Steve Borthwick's side in their first three Six Nations matches this year.

However, he was not included in the squad for this summer's Nations Championship Test matches, or the 36-man training squad for this autumn's fixtures, despite being part of Northampton's Prem title success.

Rugby.body:
South Africa centre Damian de Allende has singled out Jordie Barrett as the current rival who “really does stand out” to him after going head-to-head with the All Blacks star during Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

The 101-cap Springbok has faced some of the finest centres of the modern era during his international career, highlighting battles with Ma’a Nonu, Conrad Smith and Sonny Bill Williams, as well as compatriots Frans Steyn, Andre Esterhuizen and Jan Serfontein.

Rugby.summary: World Rugby would help any nation which wants to switch a Six Nations match to the United States as it continues its drive to spread the game stateside.
Rugby.body:
World Rugby would help any nation which wants to switch a Six Nations match to the United States, as it continues its drive to spread the game stateside. South Africa and New Zealand have sold out the 71,000-capacity M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore for Saturday's fourth and final Test in their Greatest Rivalry series.

With the men's and women's Rugby World Cups being held in the United States in 2031 and 2033 respectively, tournament organisers are keen to bring more prestige fixtures across the Atlantic.

Rugby.title: Two-time Olympic medallist to make Test debut for Canada against Scotland
Rugby.summary: Two-time Olympic medallist Charity Williams will make her Test rugby debut against Scotland in Canada's WXV Global Series opener in Edinburgh.
Rugby.body:
Two-time Olympic medallist Charity Williams will make her Test rugby debut against Scotland in Canada’s WXV Global Series opener in Edinburgh. The 29-year-old has competed in rugby sevens at three Olympic Games, winning a bronze medal in 2016 and silver in Paris two years ago.

She is joined by current Canada Women’s Sevens teammate Savannah Bauder in the squad. Williams starts on the left wing in a back three that also contains Fancy Bermudez and Claire Gallagher.

Women’s Rugby World Cup-winning prop Kelsey Clifford has been ruled out of the Red Roses’ home WXV Global Series fixtures. The 24-year-old Saracens prop will miss Test matches against Australia, Canada and New Zealand’s Black Ferns in September with a hamstring injury.

Clifford will remain as part of the Red Roses training squad with a view to returning for the team’s two matches against Canada and the fixture against the USA Women’s Eagles in October.

Rugby.summary: Having coached in the Top 14 with Montpellier, I always like to keep an eye on affairs in France. With the first round of games, the standout fixture was La Rochelle’s last-gasp 30-27 win over superclub, Toulouse.
Rugby.body:
Having coached in the Top 14 with Montpellier, I always like to keep an eye on affairs in France. With the first round of games, the standout fixture was La Rochelle’s last-gasp 30-27 win over superclub, Toulouse.

At the end of the game, Ugo Mola, their head coach, was apoplectic. He’d seen his star-studded side lose to Ronan O’Gara’s men with the last kick of the match. What was interesting was his ire was directed squarely at his bench and the lack of impact they’d made in the game. He lambasted them.

Rugby.title: SA Rugby hail ‘leading coach’ Swys de Bruin after Springbok Women exit
Rugby.summary: SA Rugby President, Mark Alexander, has described outgoing Springbok Women head coach Swys de Bruin as one of the "leading coaches in the country".
Rugby.body:
SA Rugby President, Mark Alexander, has described outgoing Springbok Women head coach Swys de Bruin as one of the “leading coaches in the country”. Last week, De Bruin’s resignation from the South Africa set-up was unexpectedly announced in the lead-up to their Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry encounter with the Black Ferns at Soweto’s FNB Stadium.

De Bruin initially joined the union’s high-performance department in August 2024 before being appointed Springbok Women boss. During his time in charge of the team, the 66-year-old led the Springbok Women to new heights, headlined by their run to the quarter-finals of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025. The team also ranked among the top 10 women’s rugby nations in the world for the first time.

Rugby.body:

The governing body is pressing on with controversial plans to go from four professional men's clubs to three by 2028. Rugby.title: Why Cardiff is the perfect place to kick off Ultimate Sevens
Rugby.summary: Even within the long list of internationally renowned rugby cauldrons, the Cardiff Arms Park precinct in Wales’ capital holds a unique place.
Rugby.body:
Even within the long list of internationally renowned rugby cauldrons, the Cardiff Arms Park precinct in Wales’ capital holds a unique place. As it prepares to re-enter the world of sevens rugby for the first time in over a decade with the launch of the Ultimate Sevens, the new competition is set to tread on hallowed ground, and it could not have picked a more appropriate place to acknowledge rugby’s past.

Sport in many forms has been played in the precinct along the River Taff for nearly 200 years, the original field starting out as a site for cricket matches in the 1850s. By the 1880s, rugby had arrived, the area converted into a cricket ground to the north (the site of today’s ground where the Ultimate Sevens will be played) and a rugby union ground to the south, the current home of Millennium Stadium.

Rugby.body:

The summer arrivals Nicky Smith and Tomas Francis have been taking this on. At the club’s Carrington training ground, the two Wales props compare notes on how they are going. “I was doing well until today, but Tom has cut his hair and he looks more like Ben now which threw me,” admits Francis.

Rugby.body:
1999 Rugby World Cup winner Nathan Grey is helping the USA Eagles build towards the sport’s showpiece event next year in Australia, having been announced in June as one of five assistant coaches ahead of the World Rugby Nations Cup.

Grey has brought extensive playing and coaching experience into the USA set-up, now working under Scott Lawrence as the defence coach. The 35-Test Wallaby has backed up a successful playing career by building an impressive coaching CV across more than two decades.

Rugby.title: Pia Tapsell: 'I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t a little worried about the reception'
Rugby.summary: The Black Ferns' euphoric 2022 season was a nightmare for Pia Tapsell.
Rugby.body:
The Black Ferns’ euphoric 2022 season was a nightmare for Pia Tapsell. The abrasive loose forward who started all six Tests in a successful 2019, when the Black Ferns defeated England 28-13 in San Diego en route to a Super Series title, missed selection for the Women’s Rugby World Cup. A serious ACL injury ruled her out for all of 2023.

A slow recovery and desire for a new challenge led her to move to Australia. On August 22 at North Harbour Stadium in Albany, she became the first woman to play a Test match for both the Black Ferns and the Wallaroos when she came off the bench for Australia in the last half hour of their 66-19 defeat.

Rugby.title: One-cap England winger backed a winner with black horse campaign
Rugby.summary: Lloyds Bank’s iconic black horse was front and centre of the RFU’s announcement of their new back-of-shirt sponsor on Wednesday, but it’s very presence is all thanks to a winger who won one cap against Scotland 56 years ago.
Rugby.body:
Lloyds Bank’s iconic black horse was front and centre of the RFU’s announcement of their new back-of-shirt sponsor on Wednesday, but it’s very presence is all thanks to a winger who won one cap against Scotland 56 years ago.

Mike Bulpitt was born in Richmond, Yorkshire, in April 1944 and played for Blackheath, Eastern Counties, Rosslyn Park, London Counties and the Barbarians. He worked for the ad agency Coleman Prentice & Varley before joining Lloyds Bank as Assistant Advertising Manager, where he developed the bank’s famous ‘Black Horse’ campaign. He was chief manager of marketing communications when he retired.

Rugby.title: World Rugby confirm pathway to 2028 Olympic Sevens with superstars eyeing LA28
Rugby.summary: World Rugby have confirmed the qualification route for rugby sevens at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, with 12 men’s and 12 women’s teams set to compete and the race for places beginning on the 2027 HSBC SVNS circuit.
Rugby.body:
World Rugby have confirmed the qualification route for rugby sevens at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, with 12 men’s and 12 women’s teams set to compete and the race for places beginning on the 2027 HSBC SVNS circuit.

Hosts USA are guaranteed a place in both competitions, while the four highest-ranked eligible teams in the men’s and women’s 2027 SVNS World Championship standings will also qualify automatically. The campaign begins in Dubai in November 2026 and concludes in Bordeaux at the end of May.

Rugby.title: Borthwick's holding pattern extended
Rugby.summary: England head coach Steve Borthwick's extra six months buys time but doesn't indicate reserves of confidence from his Rugby Football Union employers.
Rugby.body:
"Horrendous" is not a word anyone wants to hear in their appraisal. It was, however, the one chosen by Conor O'Shea, the man responsible for overseeing England's international success, to describe the men's team's 2026 Six Nations campaign.

And many fans will find it entirely apt. England won only one match, their worst return since the tournament's expansion a quarter of a century ago. They lacked cohesion, discipline and tactical variety. It prompted profound, widespread questions about the future of head coach Steve Borthwick.

The Indian senior women’s rugby sevens team has commenced a national camp at the Sports Authority of India’s Netaji Subhas Eastern Centre in Kolkata as part of its final preparations for the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. The team will compete in the women’s rugby sevens tournament at the Paloma Mizuho Rugby Stadium in Nagoya from October 1 to 3. India is placed in Pool B alongside defending champions China, Hong Kong, China, and Malaysia.

Rugby.body:
With the Top14 already underway, the Ligue Nationale de Rugby has released the salary cap figures for each club for the 2026/2027 season. The competition’s base budget is €11.1 million, a figure that may increase depending on how many players are involved with the French national 15s and 7s squads.

The reigning champions, Stade Toulousain, have the largest salary cap budget in the competition, reaching €13.8 million, which is driven by the club having 16 players who have represented the French national team in the past season – 15 in the 15s and one in the 7s.

Rugby.title: 'Talent, neglect and deprivation'
Rugby.summary: Through apartheid, poverty and financial crises, this special province continues to defy the odds, but investment is needed to stop it being left behind.
Rugby.body:
Around the jagged cliffs of Coffee Bay, the Wild Coast earns its name. Undulating green hills plunge from great heights into a frothing sea. Fat oysters cling to the surf-battered rocks. The sandy beaches are vast, the water brilliant and the views staggering.

The roads in and out are less romantic. They turn to porridge when it rains and are pocked with potholes beneath the baking sun. Coffee Bay is a place that can take your breath away, provided you are only passing through.

Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter admits he was delighted to see full-back Tommy Wyatt put almost two years of injury hell behind him and is now ready to accelerate his progress ahead of the new season.

Wyatt played 40 minutes of a pre-season game against the Scarlets last weekend, his first game in over a year after suffering a second serious knee ligament injury. Baxter says that, as expected for someone who has been out of action for such a long period, Wyatt made some errors as he shook off the rust.

Rugby.title: ‘The All Blacks are back… and they are most certainly World Cup contenders’
Rugby.summary: Despite falling 2-1 down in their series with South Africa, New Zealand have shown they are good enough to challenge for global glory in 2027.
Rugby.body:
Regardless of how the last Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series plays out, there is enough reason now to be confident that the All Blacks are back. They are the All Blacks again. Behaving like them, training like them, preparing like them and playing like them. Once again, New Zealand are a genuine threat to every team they play and good enough to beat everyone on any given day.

They are, most certainly, World Cup contenders and just how strong a chance they are of winning in Australia depends on how far they progress along their current trajectory in the next 12 months.

Rugby.summary: Red Roses record try-scorer Sue Day is among the latest five World Rugby Hall of Fame inductees.
Rugby.body:
Red Roses record try-scorer Sue Day is among the latest five World Rugby Hall of Fame inductees. During a 10-year career with the Red Roses, Day scored 61 tries for England, including 19 at three Women’s Rugby World Cups. A tally only bettered by that of Portia Woodman-Wickliffe.

She also captained the Red Roses to one of the three Women’s Six Nations titles claimed during her career. Since retirement, Day has been appointed the first-ever female president of Wasps FC and as a partner at her accountancy firm.

Rugby.summary: He has won 57.4% of his Tests (28/48) as head coach since succeeding Eddie Jones, and will join double Grand Slam winner and fellow northerner Geoff Cooke on 50 Tests when England play Japan in November.
Rugby.body:
Steve Borthwick is set to be awarded a contract extension by the RFU through to 2028, according to a report in The Telegraph today. The 46-year-old Lancastrian first took charge of England ahead of the 2023 Six Nations, and led them to the semi-finals of that year’s Rugby World Cup.

He has won 57.4% of his Tests (28/48) as head coach since succeeding Eddie Jones, and will join double Grand Slam winner and fellow northerner Geoff Cooke on 50 Tests when England play Japan on Saturday, 14 November, at Allianz Stadium.

Vancouver-born Spencer Jones spent his teenage years living in New Zealand, coming through the rugby age-grade ranks in Waikato before opting to take a break from the sport. It was a choice that led to life-changing opportunities and “sparked that love again” for rugby.

Rugby.summary: Exeter boss Rob Baxter hopes full-back Tommy Wyatt can return to his best form after overcoming his second serious knee injury.
Rugby.body:
Exeter boss Rob Baxter hopes full-back Tommy Wyatt can return to his best form after overcoming his second serious knee injury. The 26-year-old returned to action last weekend in Exeter's pre-season friendly loss to Scarlets at Sandy Park, where he played the first half.

He missed the entirety of last season after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee in the final game of the 2024-25 campaign. Wyatt had missed much of 2024 having suffered a similar injury in his other knee.

Rugby.title: Rugby Union Weekly
Rugby.summary: Ugo and Chris chat to RFU performance director Conor O'Shea.
Rugby.body: Ugo and Chris sit down with the RFU performance director Conor O’Shea for a wide-ranging conversation about the big issues shaping English rugby. O’Shea reveals they plan to extend Steve Borthwick’s contract to cover the 2028 Six Nations and prevent speculation around his future. They discuss the importance of the upcoming autumn and despite a poor 2026 O’Shea tells us England can go all the way at the 2027 World Cup in Australia. Should the RFU scrap the rule preventing overseas-based players being picked for England? And how do they improve the coaching pathway for English coaches to make the jump from domestic to international rugby? They also quiz O’Shea on the Red Roses’ dominance and the succession plan for John Mitchell.

Rugby.title: Tamaiti Williams offers encouraging return update after scary back injury
Rugby.summary: The 27 Test All Blacks prop is on an upward trajectory to return to the Christchurch-based Super Rugby Pacific franchise in 2027.
Rugby.body:
Injured All Blacks prop Tamaiti Williams has provided an update on his recovery from a serious back injury during the Crusaders’ 2026 Super Rugby Pacific season. The 26-year-old played 104 minutes for the Crusaders in 2026, missing the rest of the Super Rugby Pacific campaign and the international season to date.

Williams was suspended after their round three clash with the Chiefs, before his week off was cut short by severe back pain. While the initial injury seemed minor, as the weeks went by, Williams was forced into hospital for a chunk of time over a couple of months.

Rugby.summary: Uganda steps up preparations to host World Rugby Sevens qualifiers The Eastleigh Voice
Rugby.body:
Uganda has stepped up preparations to host a qualification tournament for the 2027 World Rugby Sevens Series. The two-day tournament, scheduled for September 26-27, will feature eight teams and serve as the opening leg of the 2026/2027 men's World Rugby Sevens qualifying series.

Godwin Kayangwe, president of the Uganda Rugby Union (URU), told Xinhua on Monday that the union was working closely with the government to ensure the tournament's success. "We are confident that Uganda will host an excellent tournament and we are preparing well for it," added Kayangwe.

Rugby.title: 2026 WXV Global Series preview: Scotland
Rugby.summary: When the WXV Global Series fixtures were first being arranged, Scotland would have been delighted to secure fixtures versus Canada and New Zealand at home first up.
Rugby.body:
When the WXV Global Series fixtures were first being arranged, Scotland would have been delighted to secure fixtures versus Canada and New Zealand at home first up. After all, those sides are lying number three and number two in the world ranking respectively at time of writing, will bring the crowds flocking to Hive Stadium in Edinburgh and Canada were last in Scotland in 2018 and the Black Ferns have never played in the country.

Both games will certainly be glamour days and big occasions for women’s rugby in Scotland that’s for sure, but fast forward a few months since the fixtures were made public and the Scots might fancy a slightly less taxing start to their five-game September and October schedule.

Rugby.title: 2026 WXV Global Series preview: The Wallaroos
Rugby.summary: Of all the teams taking part in the WXV Global Series, the Wallaroos come into September in one of the most intriguing positions in all of international women’s rugby.
Rugby.body:
Of all the teams taking part in the WXV Global Series, the Wallaroos come into September in one of the most intriguing positions in all of international women’s rugby. These eight weeks will mark the final time the Wallaroos take the field as semi-professional athletes – with XVs players joining their sevens counterparts in a full-time, high-performance environment from November.

Led by the new Head of Women’s High Performance, Tim Walsh, morale on the ground is high: with the Australia Sevenss winning the 2026 HSBC SVNS World Championship and the governing body having one eye on the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles and Women’s Rugby World Cup 2029 on home soil.

Rugby.summary: Tom Pearson says that Northampton Saints will have a target on their back as they bid to become the first team since Saracens in 2019 to retain their Gallagher PREM crown.
Rugby.body:
Tom Pearson says that Northampton Saints will have a target on their back as they bid to become the first team since Saracens in 2019 to retain their Gallagher PREM crown. The North London side have been crowned back-to-back champions twice in the last decade, and England A back-rower Pearson, 26, knows nine clubs will be looking to knock Saints off their perch.

Pearson believes Saints, who have won two of the last three PREM finals at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium, will be helped in their quest to become top dogs again after keeping most of their squad intact.

Rugby.summary: Rugby Canada have struck a strategic deal with Champ Rugby in England to enable their players to get more competitive game time in the lead up to Rugby World Cup 2027.
Rugby.body:
Rugby Canada have struck a strategic deal with Champ Rugby in England to enable their players to get more competitive game time in the lead up to Rugby World Cup 2027. Financial and logistical measures have been put in place to encourage clubs to sign Canadian players and reverse the trend of recent years.

Canadian players used to be prevalent in the second-tier Champ until the introduction of English-qualified conditional funding put clubs off signing players from North America.

Rugby.summary: Springbok Women co-coach Laurian Johannes-Haupt believes her side “established credibility” despite a 52-20 defeat to the Black Ferns at FNB Stadium.
Rugby.body:
Springbok Women co-coach Laurian Johannes-Haupt believes her side “established credibility” despite a 52-20 defeat to the Black Ferns at FNB Stadium. For the opening 30 minutes in the curtain-raiser to Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry’s third Test, the Springbok Women were well in the contest. Their forward pack posed physical questions to Whitney Hansen’s team.

It was not quite the effort of their Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 exploits against the same opposition. Almost a year ago South Africa went in level with the Black Ferns at the break. This time around New Zealand led 24-10.

Rugby.summary: Dan McFarland arrived in the North East this summer after winning the Japanese Top League title with Kobelco Steelers.
Rugby.body:
Dan McFarland is honest enough to admit he doesn’t know what his new-look Newcastle Red Bulls squad, with 23 new signings, can achieve this season. McFarland arrived in the North East this summer after winning the Japanese Top League title with Kobelco Steelers and is trying to mould a squad that he hopes will be able to climb off the foot of the Gallagher PREM table.

The Red Bulls have won only four PREM games in three seasons, so the task is huge, but at least McFarland is honest enough not to set unrealistic goals for his side, saying it has all the feel of a start-up project.

Rugby.summary: Former Wales and Lions wing Shane Williams says pathways support for schools and colleges from the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) is 'almost non-existent'.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales and British and Irish Lions wing Shane Williams says financial support for schools and colleges rugby from the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) is "almost non-existent". Wales' record try scorer is head of rugby at Ysgol Dyffryn Aman and suggests that support is reserved for elite players tied to regions.

The 49-year-old warns that good players are being lost because of a lack of WRU investment in student pathways. "It's the most important part of it all," Williams told Radio Wales Breakfast.

Rugby.title: John Smit makes huge all-time Malcolm Marx claim ahead of All Blacks finale
Rugby.summary: Former South Africa captain John Smit has declared Malcolm Marx not only the best player in the world, but the greatest hooker to have ever played for the Springboks.
Rugby.body:
Former South Africa captain John Smit has declared Malcolm Marx not only the best player in the world, but the greatest hooker to have ever played for the Springboks. Marx was again influential in South Africa’s latest win over the All Blacks, producing a near-complete display in the 29-24 victory in Johannesburg. His lineout throwing was faultless, he won a crucial breakdown penalty and scored off a driving maul late on as the world champions opened up a 2-1 lead in the four-match series against New Zealand.

The 32-year-old has become one of the defining figures of this Springbok era, and Smit, himself a World Cup-winning hooker, believes Marx now stands above every South African to have previously worn the jersey.

Rugby.summary: Raffi Quirke says leaving Sale Sharks was one of the hardest decisions he has had to make, but is impressed with how things are taking shape at a revamped Newcastle Red Bulls.
Rugby.body:
Scrum-half Raffi Quirke says that leaving Sale Sharks was one of the hardest decisions he has ever had to make, but has been impressed with how things are taking shape at a revamped Newcastle Red Bulls.

Quirke is one of 25 new arrivals at Kingston Park, with the Red Bull ownership looking to improve on a team which has finished bottom of the table for the past four seasons. The move north means stepping away from his boyhood side and familiar surroundings, but the 25-year-old is excited by the challenge of pushing Newcastle forward in a new era for the club.

Rugby.title: England Rugby announce addition to November fixture schedule
Rugby.summary: International rugby is returning to Bath, with The Recreation Ground set to host England A vs Argentina XV on Friday, 6 November.
Rugby.body:
International rugby is returning to Bath, with The Recreation Ground set to host England A vs Argentina XV on Friday, 6 November, kick off 19:45pm (GMT). It will be the first meeting between each union’s development sides since 2009 and the third overall. England ‘A’ previously beat Argentina ‘A’ 22-17 at Franklin’s Gardens in December 1996 and again in the Churchill Cup in Colorado in June 2009 (28-20).

Argentina XV are currently licking their wounds after losing their Americas Rugby Championship crown to Chile at the weekend. Since being reintroduced in 2024, England A have played six fixtures, with five wins and a defeat. That loss was 12 months ago in England A’s only previous outing at The Rec, with the All Blacks XV winning 31-14.
Rugby.copy:
International rugby is returning to Bath, with The Recreation Ground set to host England A vs Argentina XV on Friday, 6 November, kick off 19:45pm (GMT). It will be the first meeting between each union’s development sides since 2009 and the third overall. England ‘A’ previously beat Argentina ‘A’ 22-17 at Franklin’s Gardens in December 1996 and again in the Churchill Cup in Colorado in June 2009 (28-20).

Argentina XV are currently licking their wounds after losing their Americas Rugby Championship crown to Chile at the weekend. Since being reintroduced in 2024, England A have played six fixtures, with five wins and a defeat. That loss was 12 months ago in England A’s only previous outing at The Rec, with the All Blacks XV winning 31-14.

Rugby.title: 'He looks very good, we're expecting a lot from him'
Rugby.summary: Rob Baxter has tipped 22-year-old centre Zack Wimbush for a big season as Exeter Chiefs look to fill the void left by Len Ikitau at Sandy Park ahead of the new Gallagher PREM campaign.
Rugby.body:
Rob Baxter has tipped 22-year-old centre Zack Wimbush for a breakthrough season as Exeter Chiefs look to fill the void left by Len Ikitau at Sandy Park ahead of the new Gallagher PREM campaign.

The 112kg centre, who qualifies for both England and Wales, was largely limited to PREM Cup appearances last season alongside a loan spell with Plymouth Albion. But after what Baxter has described as a “very, very good pre-season”, the Exeter boss expects him to kick on this term.

Rugby.title: Four lessons Australia need to learn from Argentina series ‘win’
Rugby.summary: Despite starting his tenure with an unbeaten run of four Tests, Les Kiss's Wallabies will need to be a lot better in the tougher assignments next up.
Rugby.body:
Coaches love to say you learn far more from a loss than a win, and even more again from a close loss. But despite starting his tenure as Australia coach with an unbeaten run that now extends to four Tests across two mini-series, Les Kiss will have collected pages of lessons from the Wallabies’ tour of Argentina.

Clearly, there’s some tough outings coming up next and it’s not an earth-shattering revelation to suggest they will need to be a lot better than we’ve seen over the last six weeks with South Africa up next, then New Zealand twice, before four more Nations Championship matches in November – England, Scotland, Wales, plus a play-off match.

Rugby.title: Ex-Wales captain secures ‘key’ WRU development role
Rugby.summary: Former Wales captain Siwan Lillicrap has been appointed head of women's coaching and development by the Welsh Rugby Union.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales captain Siwan Lillicrap has been appointed head of women’s coaching and development by the Welsh Rugby Union. The role, which has been newly created, is one that the WRU have described as “key” and “acknowledges the rapid growth of the women’s and girls’ game globally”. It is also forms part of the WRU’s ‘One Wales’ strategy.

During a six year international career, Lillicrap won 51 caps for Wales and has been Pathway Manager for the three Player Development Centres established by the WRU in Wast Wales, West Wales and North Wales since 2023. She was also Wales Women’s Under-18s head coach.

Rugby.title: Historic result in South America as Chile complete stunning comeback
Rugby.summary: This year marked the return of the Americas Rugby Championship, which had been forced into a long hiatus due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Rugby.body:
The 2026 Americas Rugby Championship concluded at the weekend, and Chile XV took the title home after successfully defeating Uruguay XV, Paraguay and Argentina XV. This year marked the return of the tournament, which had been forced into a long hiatus due to the COVID-19 pandemic; Argentina XV won the last edition held in 2019.

While Chile, Uruguay and Argentina competed with their secondary sides, the Cóndores and Los Teros still fielded several of their main players, including Chilean siblings Santiago and Benjamín Videla and Uruguayan back-rower Manuel Diana.

Rugby.title: Ollie Blyth-Lafferty: 'I had my plumber's tool bag ready to go, then Edinburgh offered me a contract'
Rugby.summary: The 135kg would-be plumber is only 20, but has all the raw materials to become the cornterstone of Scotland's pack in the years ahead.
Rugby.body:
Had things turned out a little differently, Ollie Blyth-Lafferty would be servicing boilers instead of grinding at the coalface of rugby’s least forgiving frontier. The enormous tighthead prop, who thundered onto the URC scene last season, had his heart set on becoming a plumber before rugby jolted suddenly from hobby to career path. In the past nine months, the 20-year-old has signed his first professional contract, captained Scotland U20s, and played 15 games for Edinburgh, four of them in the Champions Cup. His first start came in a sterling win opposite Toulon’s gnarled loosehead Jean-Baptiste Gros. His immense 6ft 4ins, 135kg frame is a precious rarity in Scotland. His clear zest for scrummaging and the dearth of options to back up Zander Fagerson have fuelled clamour for him to be capped at Test level. The mending of leaks and unclogging of toilets, then, can wait.

“I was planning on leaving school at 16 to do plumbing and heating,” Blyth-Lafferty says. “I had a start day lined up, I had my own tool bag ready to go, and then I got offered a senior academy contract with Edinburgh and that was full time. I couldn’t go into plumbing.

Rugby.title: Wallaroos embrace ultimate test against ‘gold standard’ of women’s 15s
Rugby.summary: Desiree Miller believes the Aussies can go into their WXV Global Series opener against England with a nothing-to-lose mentality.
Rugby.body:
Record-setting Wallaroos winger Desiree Miller believes the Aussies can go into their WXV Global Series opener against England with a nothing-to-lose mentality, as they look to take down the “gold standard” side in women’s 15s rugby.

England were beaten in the 2022 Women’s Rugby World Cup Final against New Zealand at Eden Park, but have gone unbeaten since then. The Red Roses stormed home to win the World Cup on home soil last year, and backed that up with more Six Nations success.

Rugby.title: RC Vannes: The beating heart of Bretagne set on joining the French elite
Rugby.summary: The first Breton club to win promotion to the Top 14 two years ago, Vannes are determined to make their new stay in the premier division last.
Rugby.body:
If you happen to be strolling by the Rue du Port in Vannes on a matchday, you might hear a chant sung in unison from the La Rabine stadium that will make your soul tingle. For rugby fans, while the lyrics may be unfamiliar, the melody itself will carry resonance. This is the ‘Bro Gozh ma Zadoù’, the Breton version of ‘Land of My Fathers’, Vannes and Bretagne’s official anthem which shares a common link with Wales.

Vannes, one of the oldest towns in France, first established by the Veneti, a Gallic tribe from BC times, harbours some of the most passionate and humble people and rugby clubs you will ever come across.

Rugby.summary: Rennie isn't shying away from the facts surrounding the set-piece, but knows there are areas where the All Blacks can improve.
Rugby.body:
Dave Rennie has admitted his All Blacks side is still showing signs of growing pains in both the lineout and scrum battles, where they have been tested heavily during Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour.

Rassie Erasmus’ Springboks have been ferocious and clinical at set-piece when handed the opportunities, taking advantage of the All Blacks’ indiscretions around the field. The 62-year-old All Blacks head coach explained to media in Washington, DC, and on the DSPN Podcast that his side’s inexperienced players will be better off after the gruelling seven-week tour of the Republic.

Rugby.summary: Former World Rugby Player of the Year nominee Joe Taufete’e is among the 30 Major League Rugby players named in the USA squad.

Former World Rugby Player of the Year nominee Joe Taufete’e is among the 30 Major League Rugby players named in the USA squad for the 2026 Pacific Nations Cup, which kicks off this weekend with a double-header in Osaka.

Rugby.title: Trying to withstand the Springboks shove is not working
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks on the other hand, are trying to withstand the shove, a passive approach. They want a stable platform and are trying to bunker down and withstand the heat.
Rugby.body:
The third Test between the All Blacks and Springboks once again highlighted the key difference at scrum time, which proved to be an advantage for South Africa. They won four penalties off the scrum, rewarded for their dominance, which put the spotlight back on the All Blacks’ ball handling.

Every knock-on is amplified against South Africa; the clock is lost and 30-40 metres of territory nearly every time when a penalty is conceded. You don’t just lose possession; you lose pressure, territory and momentum as well.

Rugby.title: Erasmus stays consistent with just two changes for Springboks in Baltimore
Rugby.summary: The Springboks have named their 23 to play the All Blacks in Baltimore, sticking firm with most of the starting team that secured a 2-1 lead at FNB Stadium.
Rugby.body:
The Springboks have named their 23 to play the All Blacks in Baltimore, sticking firm with most of the starting team that secured a 2-1 lead at FNB Stadium. Damian Willemse comes back into the starting team at fullback to replace Cheslin Kolbe, who was forced off early in the third Test. Willemse himself came off in the second Test with a hamstring issue.

Scrumhalf Morne van den Berg has been handed a start in the halves next to Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, with Cobus Reinach moving to the bench. The forward pack remains unchanged with Ox Nche, Malcolm Marx and Wilco Louw in the front row, Eben Etzebeth and Ruan Nortje in the second row and captain Siya Kolisi, Pieter-Steph du Toit and Jasper Wiese in the back row.

Rugby.summary: As Delaney Burns hopes to be selected to face Australia, she talks to BBC Sport about another opportunity to add to her six caps in a so-far whirlwind career.
Rugby.body:
Delaney Burns revealed to her England team-mates that at 15 years old she had a 'short back and sides' - it went down well. Rugby.title: Wales drop to lowest-ever position in the World Rugby rankings
Rugby.summary: Wales have dropped to their lowest-ever position in the World Rugby rankings after Fiji beat Japan last weekend.
Rugby.body:
Wales have dropped to their lowest-ever position in the World Rugby rankings after Fiji beat Japan last weekend. On Friday afternoon in Fukuoka, Willie Walker’s Fijiana XV were able to grind out a 15-12 win against their hosts, the Sakura Fifteen and overtake the side they stunned in the group stage of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025.

The result means that Fiji have moved to a new high of 12th in the World Rugby rankings, while Wales have fallen to their lowest ranking ever [13th]. Wales have not won a Test since July 2025, when they overcame Australia 21-12 in Brisbane. At Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 Sean Lynn’s team went winless and concluded the tournament with a 28-25 loss to Fiji. In the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations the side picked up a third wooden spoon in a row.

Rugby.title: Allow overseas stars to play for England
Rugby.summary: England selection should no longer be restricted to players based at domestic clubs, according to cap centurion Courtney Lawes.
Rugby.body:
England selection should no longer be restricted to players based at domestic clubs, according to cap centurion Courtney Lawes. The 37-year-old is back in contention to add to his 105 England appearances, having signed a one-year deal with Sale after two seasons at Brive in the French second tier.

A clutch of English talent - notably Toulouse star Jack Willis - remain across the Channel and out of reach for England head coach Steve Borthwick. "I can see why they do it because they don't want all their players playing abroad, but I don't think that's necessarily going to be the case anyway," said Lawes.

Rugby.body:
Former captain Siwan Lillicrap has been appointed as head of women's coaching and development by the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU). WRU chiefs say Lillicrap will "deliver an aligned coaching and development system across the women's performance pathway for players between 14 and 24 years of age" in the newly created role.

Lillicrap, who won 51 Wales caps, has worked as WRU's pathway manager and women's under-18s head coach since retiring from international rugby in 2022. In her role as pathways manager, the 38-year-old oversaw player development centres in east, west and north Wales.

Lotte Sharp has re-signed with Saracens to take her association with the North London club into a 13th season. The 31-year-old joined Saracens in 2014 from Welwyn Rugby and won the Women’s Premiership in her first season.

Rugby.title: Henry Pollock contract call a win for everyone – Andy Goode
Rugby.summary: Henry Pollock’s new contract at Northampton represents a win for everyone, even if it might not be worth the million pound a year that Eddie Hearn was after.
Rugby.body:
Henry Pollock’s new contract at Northampton represents a win for everyone, even if it might not be worth the million pounds a year that Eddie Hearn was after. Let’s face it, the reported Newcastle offer came about because I don’t think anyone expects him to move abroad at his age and they’re the only club in the PREM who could offer him anywhere near that amount of money.

Pollock wants to win things, develop his own game and make an even bigger impression on the international stage though, as well as earning as much as possible along the way, and there’s absolutely no doubt that Saints is the right place for him.

Rugby.summary: The fly-half entered the fray after Cheslin Kolbe broke his jaw, and turned the Springboks from ball winners to ball users against the All Blacks.
Rugby.body:
A traditional proverb: “better to be lucky than good”. Even at the elite level of sporting performance, where every ‘i’ is dotted and every ‘t’ is crossed, sometimes you need to catch a lucky break for all the preparation to count. Life can be that simple.

As the American crooner Frank Sinatra once observed, “people often remark I’m pretty lucky. Luck is only important insofar as getting the chance to sell yourself at the right moment. After that, you’ve got to have talent and know how to use it.”

Rugby.title: Where does PREM Cup points-fest rank in rugby's highest-scoring matches?
Rugby.summary: It was a truly remarkable opening weekend of the PREM Rugby Cup, with an aggregate of 365 points scored across the four matches.
Rugby.body:
It was a truly remarkable opening weekend of the PREM Rugby Cup, with an aggregate of 365 points scored across the four matches. On any other weekend, the point-a-minute, 43-40 thriller between Bristol and Gloucester, won by the Bears, would have likely eclipsed all others as a free-for-all.

But at the same time as they were going at each other hammer and tongs in the west, Saracens and Northampton served up a scoreline that was barely believable. Twenty tries were scored – 14 to Saracens and six to Northampton – with young Jack Bracken claiming a nine-minute hat-trick.

Rugby.summary: Charlie Bracken, son of RWC 2003 winner and fellow scrum-half Kyran, has been called into this week's three-day alignment camp.
Rugby.body:
Charlie Bracken, son of RWC 2003 winner and fellow scrum-half Kyran, has been called into England’s three-day alignment camp after Archie McParland was forced to withdraw due to illness.

Bracken, 22, was a regular starter for England U20s in 2022 and 2023 and is now on Steve Borthwick’s radar for the senior team. He has played just over 50 games for Saracens since making his debut in the 2021/22 season, having spent some time on loan at Ampthill in the Champ.

Rugby.summary: The Newcastle Red Bulls flyer has touched down 95 times in the PREM.
Rugby.body:
Christian Wade is determined to enjoy becoming the highest try-scorer in PREM history if he eventually passes Chris Ashton, knowing it might not be long before someone comes along and knocks him off the top spot.

The Newcastle Red Bulls flyer has touched down 95 times in the PREM and is six short of Ashton’s mark, which he would likely have passed long ago but for spells in the NFL, France and Rugby League.

Rugby.title: Camborne impress in opening game in National One
Rugby.summary: Camborne are capable of taking on the top teams in National One after winning their first game since promotion, says coach Ricky Pellow.
Rugby.body:
Camborne are capable of taking on the top teams in National One after winning their first game since promotion, says coach Ricky Pellow. The Cornish side came back from 29-14 down at half time to run out 38-36 winners at Leeds Tykes to begin their campaign in the third tier with a bonus-point victory.

Ben Priddey scored two tries, while Josh Matavesi, Alex Ducker and Ben Prisk also scored as full-back Rory O'Kane scored the decisive penalty late on. "You look at the age of the squad, and there's a lot of young players in there that have played their first game for the club and also Nat One, so they're going to learn a lot," Camborne sporting director and former Exeter skills coach Pellow told BBC Radio Cornwall.
