Rugby.summary: England fly-half Fin Smith has revealed the tough lesson Northampton Saints learned from their 2023/24 Gallagher PREM triumph as the champions prepare to defend the title they reclaimed last season.
Rugby.body:
England fly-half Fin Smith has revealed the tough lesson Northampton Saints learned from their 2023/24 Gallagher PREM triumph as the champions prepare to defend the title they reclaimed last season.

Despite reaching the Investec Champions Cup final in 2025, they mounted a dismal title defence, finishing in eighth place. Smith admits Saints became too consumed by trying to recreate their previous success after winning the league, with the squad repeatedly looking back at what had worked rather than finding ways to evolve.

Rugby.title: Anscombe's Scarlets debut delayed by paperwork
Rugby.summary: Scarlets hope Gareth Anscombe can debut against Dragons on Friday after a registration issue prevented him from playing against Exeter Chiefs.
Rugby.body:
Scarlets hope Gareth Anscombe can make his debut against Dragons on Friday after a registration issue prevented him from playing against Exeter Chiefs. The 35-year-old fly-half had been named to start the pre-season game at Sandy Park last weekend but was withdrawn shortly before kick-off.

Scarlets have confirmed the former Wales international was not injured and that the issue is related to his registration. The club are hopeful the paperwork will be resolved swiftly, with Anscombe set to play against Dragons at Church Bank, Llandovery on 11 September if he is cleared in time.

Rugby.body:
John Mitchell has named a 36-player WXV Global Series squad featuring 25 Women’s Rugby World Cup winners. The team named for their three home fixtures in September, continues to be captained by Meg Jones in the absence of pregnant Zoe Stratford, contains three uncapped players and has a combined total of 1,234 Test caps.

Rugby.summary: Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has backed Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu to be the Springboks first-choice fly-half moving forward, but has said he "needs to work through this second-year syndrome."
Rugby.body:
Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has backed Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu to be the Springboks’ first-choice fly-half going forward, but has said he “needs to work through this second-year syndrome.”

The 24-year-old has started all three Tests of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series so far, but was originally dropped to the bench for the second Test in Cape Town before Handre Pollard, who was scheduled to start, pulled out through injury.

Rugby.title: Smaller ball for women makes it 'harder to do my job'
Rugby.summary: A smaller ball is being trialled in women's international rugby union for September and October's WXV Global Series - and it is dividing opinion.
Rugby.body:
England will play Australia, Canada and New Zealand in the next three weeks and, like all the world's top women's players, they have some new equipment: a smaller ball. During September and October's WXV Global Series, World Rugby is trialling a size 4.5 ball - about 3% smaller than the size five used in the men's game, but the same weight.

Their introduction has not been without controversy and for England hooker May Campbell, responsible for throwing the ball in at the line-out, told BBC Sport it can go "a bit skew-whiff".

Rugby.title: Mike Blair frustrated after another Test plagued by missed 'opportunities'
Rugby.summary: Blair felt that the All Blacks put the experienced Springboks players under pressure at times, but couldn't capitalise on the momentum shifts in the 80-minute contest.
Rugby.body:
Creating opportunities, but not finishing them. That’s the feeling from All Blacks assistant coach Mike Blair, who feels that at FNB Stadium, they put themselves in the right positions but couldn’t capitalise on those chances.

Blair’s admission follows the All Blacks’ 29-24 defeat to the Springboks in Soweto, where the home side were clinical in pouncing on the visitors’ mistakes. Dave Rennie’s All Blacks started the better of the two heavyweight sides, but couldn’t survive the brutal power game the Springboks threw at them.

Rugby.title: The five moments that cost the All Blacks in Soweto
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks had plenty of chances in the third Test in South Africa to claim a historic 2-1 result on South African soil.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks had plenty of chances in the third Test in South Africa to claim a historic 2-1 result on South African soil. After going up by 12-5 in the first half and 17-12 in the second half, the game was for the taking but a number of key opportunities lost didn’t build the required buffer on the scoreboard.

Dave Rennie’s side continually turn one error into a handful, leading to huge momentum swings against them. Their inability to effectively win restarts was a huge issue in this series.

Rugby.title: Wales lock Carter cleared for Dragons after injury
Rugby.summary: Dragons co-captain Ben Carter fit for start of United Rugby Championship season after recovering from ankle injury he sustained with Wales.
Rugby.body:
Dragons co-captain Ben Carter will be fit for the start of the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship (URC) after recovering from an ankle injury he sustained with Wales. The lock was ruled out of the Nations Championship defeat by South Africa in mid-July after a blow in training.

Carter, who had started Wales' six previous games, was on crutches and saw specialists on his return to Dragons. The 25-year-old did not need surgery and is working towards his side's URC opener at Benetton on Friday, 25 September (19:45 BST).

Rugby.summary: "You can't hide from it? Their set piece is pretty damn dominant, and they get a gravy train of penalties from it," Barnes admitted.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks assistant coach Neil Barnes isn’t hiding away from the Springboks’ set-piece dominance in Soweto, admitting he and scrum coach Jason Ryan have work to do. The All Blacks fell to their second straight defeat for the first time since 2024, and their second loss under new head coach Dave Rennie, who has now coached the All Blacks in six Tests and four midweek games.

Rennie’s side will look to level the four-Test series in Baltimore this weekend, as they stare down the barrel of a 3-1 series defeat at the hands of the back-to-back World Champions.

Rugby.title: All Blacks trim squad for Baltimore as nine players return home
Rugby.summary: Rennie said All Blacks midfielder Quinn Tupaea was also unlikely to feature after picking up an MCL injury in the second half.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks have landed in Baltimore ahead of the fourth and final Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series for 2026, but will be without nine squad members. Head coach Dave Rennie announced post-match, after their 29-24 defeat in Soweto against the Springboks, that Ardie Savea was ruled out of the Baltimore Test with a shoulder injury.

Rennie said All Blacks midfielder Quinn Tupaea was also unlikely to feature after picking up an MCL injury in the second half. After the press conferences, it was announced on social media that All Blacks vice-captain Luke Jacobson would also miss the fourth Test in Soweto with an elbow tendon issue.

Rugby.title: Rassie Erasmus on scrum battle between Boks and All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Springboks head coach has complimented the All Blacks scrum in the wake of the 29-24 win Soweto in the third Test of the Greatest Rivalry series.
Rugby.body:
Springboks head coach has complimented the All Blacks scrum in the wake of the 29-24 win Soweto in the third Test of the Greatest Rivalry series. After a week marred by debate of scrum tactics and fury from the Springboks fans, the scrums were in South Africa’s favour in Soweto.

The All Blacks conceded 12 penalties, many of which were at scrum time giving the Springboks an exit and territorial gain. “I think we were caught for a free kick. We were caught for collapsing one,” Erasmus said of the scrums.

Rugby.summary: Uruguayan hooker Joaquín Myszka's has been handed a 13-game ban for a red-card offence that left Chile's Emilio Shea Duret seriously injured, eight days after the incident.
Rugby.body:
Uruguayan hooker Joaquín Myszka has been handed a 13-game ban for a red-card offence that left Chile’s Emilio Shea Duret seriously injured, eight days after the incident. The incident happened in the second half of the Chile XV and Uruguay XV match for the Americas Rugby Championship, in which the Los Teros secondary team lost 33-12.

At the 52nd minute, Myszka made a low no-arms tackle to the opposing prop that resulted in a serious injury, forcing the game to be stopped for several minutes until Shea Duret was carried off the field.

helped Team Canada capture the 2026 FISU World Championship Rugby Sevens title in Stellenbosch, South Africa. Rugby.body:
Second row Maro Itoje has returned to the England set-up after being named in a 36-man training squad for this autumn's Nations Championship matches. Itoje missed matches against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina in July, taking his first proper summer break from rugby in more than a decade.

Rugby.title: Malcolm Marx is rugby's greatest bully
Rugby.summary: Then Malcolm Marx arrived his team under pressure, stooping low to dislodge the ball with a brutal...
Rugby.body:
An hour had passed in a pulsating contest in the cavernous calabash that is FNB Stadium. Minutes earlier Will Jordan had rounded a superb All Blacks move and Jesse Kriel brushed past Leroy Carter to land an instant riposte. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu’s conversion nudged the Springboks ahead for the first time. The entire series hung in the balance like a stack of Jenga tiles after one too many pieces had been removed.

Then Malcolm Marx arrived; his team under pressure, he stooped low to come up with a brutal, momentum-shifting steal. The Boks hooker shot a wagging finger and wore an expression that was less the satisfaction of a professional athlete completing a technical skill than that of a schoolyard bully mocking the unfortunate kid who had just discovered that standing up to him was a mistake.

Then Malcolm Marx arrived; his team under pressure, he stooped low to come up with a brutal, momentum-shifting steal. The Boks hooker shot a wagging finger and wore an expression that was less the satisfaction of a professional athlete completing a technical skill than that of a schoolyard bully mocking the unfortunate kid who had just discovered that standing up to him was a mistake.

Rugby.title: 'Nic White diving school': Cam Roigard under fire for tip tackle incident with Reinach
Rugby.summary: All Blacks halfback Cam Roigard has been accused of diving during the incident late in the first half with Cobus Reinach.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks halfback Cam Roigard has been accused of diving during the incident late in the first half where he was up ended by opposite No.9 Cobus Reinach. Roigard attempted to tackle Reinach at the base of the scrum, not aware initially that referee Nika Amushukeli had blown a penalty try.

When Roigard backed off, Reinach flipped him over aggressively with Roigard landing awkwardly. From the restart, the All Blacks were handed a penalty but no card was issued. Former Springbok midfielder Jean de Villiers made a point in commentary to call out Roigard for “gamesmanship”.

Rugby.body:
Australia coach Les Kiss insists the Wallabies will be “up for the fight” when they meet two-time defending Rugby World Cup winners the Springboks later this month, following a historic series win in Argentina.

Rugby.summary: The Wallabies have missed a chance to pinch victory against an undermanned Argentina in a 28-28 draw in Mendoza.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies have missed a chance to pinch victory against an undermanned Argentina in a 28-28 draw in Mendoza that still secured a historic series win against Los Pumas. Chasing a fifth-straight win and fourth in a row under new coach Les Kiss, the visitors benefited from back-to-back Argentina yellow cards for deliberate knock-ons that left the hosts two short for most of the final 10 minutes.

But with Carter Gordon also off injured – halfbacks Kalani Thomas and Ryan Lonergan acted as playmakers – the hosts coughed up possession and then knocked on as Los Pumas hung on.

Rugby.title: 'Please don't see it as boasting': Rassie Erasmus on advantage over Dave Rennie's All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus has assessed Dave Rennie's All Blacks after taking a 2-1 advantage in the Greatest Rivalry series, stressing that the series is not over.
Rugby.body:
Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus has assessed Dave Rennie’s All Blacks after taking a 2-1 advantage in the Greatest Rivalry series, stressing that the series is not over. The coach was relieved and happy to have won the third Test which means that the Springboks can’t lose the series, only win or draw the series in the fourth Test.

“They can draw it in Baltimore, and obviously we are happy tonight,” Erasmus said post-match. “So I know they lost this part in South Africa, but it’s still three games. I know they smashed us in the first one, but I thought the score was a little bit skew.

Rugby.title: The surprising Eben Etzebeth moment that caught Bok fans offguard
Rugby.summary: Chalk it down as 'something you don't see every day', at least not on a Test field when Eben Etzebeth is playing for the Springboks.
Rugby.body:
Chalk it down as ‘something you don’t see every day’, at least not on a Test field when Eben Etzebeth is playing for the Springboks. The Boks forwards eventually bullied New Zealand into submission in Soweto, securing a 29-24 victory and a 2-1 series lead. The All Blacks matched the Springboks’ intensity early, with Ardie Savea scoring twice before a shoulder injury ended his afternoon.

Will Jordan’s opportunistic try put New Zealand 17-12 ahead, but Jesse Kriel responded almost immediately, exposing a soft tackle and restoring South Africa’s momentum. From there, the Boks’ set-piece power took over. Malcolm Marx crashed over from a dominant maul after scrum pressure forced a penalty, while Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu’s boot stretched the lead to 12 points.

All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has provided an initial update on the health of both Ardie Savea and Quinn Tupaea. The two All Blacks left the field with injuries during the Springboks’ 29-24 triumph in Soweto. Savea picked up a shoulder injury from a Jasper Wiese cleanout in the 30th minute, leaving the field.

Savea contributed two five-pointers during his short stint, pouncing on Springboks’ errors. The All Blacks captain looked in severe pain, struggling to hold his right arm up on his own. Rennie confirmed post-match to Sky Sport and reporters in Johannesburg that Savea wouldn’t travel to Baltimore for the fourth and final Test match.

Rugby.body:
South Africa eventually overpowered a spirited New Zealand, who could only outrun their hosts' set-piece power for so long, as the world champions came on strong in the final quarter in Soweto to take a 2-1 lead in a high-quality 'Greatest Rivalry' series.

The two sides traded two tries each in a tight first half, with New Zealand's composure and ambition with ball in hand stretching South Africa's onrushing defence. The All Blacks sniffed a famous victory when Will Jordan chased after his own kick ahead and crossed for a 17-12 lead in the 55th minute.

Tennis.title: Could Jack Draper Follow the Path of Robin Soderling?
Tennis.summary: Could Jack Draper Follow the Path of Robin Soderling? sports.yahoo.com
Tennis.body:
- Could Jack Draper Follow the Path of Robin Soderling? The summer of 2011 should have been Robin Soderling's. He was ranked No. 4 in the world, had reached consecutive French Open finals, and had beaten Rafael Nadal at Roland Garros in 2009, the only player to do so on clay before 2015. He was 26 years old and playing some of the best tennis of his life. Then, in July, he felt something was wrong. He played on anyway.

He won the Swedish Open in Bastad, which turned out to be the last professional match he would ever play. Shortly after, he was diagnosed with mononucleosis, the viral infection that had been draining him for weeks. He tried to come back for four years. He never did.

Tennis.title: 'Red rag to a bull'
Tennis.summary: Aryna Sabalenka has lost the world number one ranking to Elena Rybakina - but has the chance to take revenge in the US Open final.
Tennis.body:
Aryna Sabalenka was fully aware she would have to win the US Open to stand any chance of stopping Elena Rybakina overtaking her as world number one. Even that would not necessarily be enough. And as the pair prepare to meet in Saturday's final, Sabalenka knows her 99-week stay at the top of the world rankings is at an end.

Kazakhstan's Rybakina is assured of replacing Sabalenka at the top of the rankings, guaranteeing that by reaching the semi-finals. Having also beaten the Belarusian to win this year's Australian Open title, Rybakina now has the opportunity to inflict further damage.

Tennis.title: US Open: Ben Shelton takes down Frances Tiafoe to seal Alexander Zverev showdown in final on Sunday in New York
Tennis.summary: US Open: Ben Shelton takes down Frances Tiafoe to seal Alexander Zverev showdown in final on Sunday in New York Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Ben Shelton defeated compatriot Frances Tiafoe in an electric US Open semi-final on Friday to secure a title showdown with Alexander Zverev. On a poignant evening that began with commemorations marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, Shelton came from a set down to beat Tiafoe 4-6 6-3 6-3 7-5 and move closer to ending a 23-year American wait for a men's singles Grand Slam champion.

No home male player has won a Grand Slam singles title since Andy Roddick triumphed in Flushing Meadows in 2003. Shelton will now have a chance to claim his maiden Grand Slam crown.

Tennis.title: American Shelton to face Zverev in US Open final
Tennis.summary: Ben Shelton powers past Frances Tiafoe in an all-American US Open semi-final to earn a spot in Sunday's final against number one seed Alexander Zverev.
Tennis.body:
Ben Shelton powered his way into the US Open final with an impressive four-set win over Frances Tiafoe in an epic all-American semi-final. Both players were bidding to reach their first Grand Slam final and put on a show for a raucous crowd on Arthur Ashe Stadium, with eighth seed Shelton coming from a set down to win 4-6 6-3 6-3 7-5.

Neither American was overawed by the occasion and they lived up to their reputations as dazzling shot-makers but, after three hours and 17 minutes, it was Shelton who won through.

Tennis.title: Hewett and Reid secure sixth US Open doubles title
Tennis.summary: British duo Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid come from a set and a break down to win the men's wheelchair doubles title for the sixth time at the US Open.
Tennis.body:
British duo Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid came from a set and a break down to win the men's wheelchair doubles title for the sixth time as a partnership at the US Open. Five years on from their most recent title at Flushing Meadows, the legendary pair battled back to beat Spain's Martin de la Puente and Ruben Spaargaren of the Netherlands 2-6 6-3 10-7 in a match tie-break.

It is a remarkable 30th Grand Slam doubles title for 34-year-old Reid, 11 years on from the Scot's first, with 26 of them coming alongside Hewett. "We've not won here for five years so this is something we've been desperate for and highly motivated for," Hewett, 28, said.

Tennis.title: Townsend & Siniakova complete career Slam in New York
Tennis.summary: Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend win the women's doubles at the US Open to complete a historic career doubles Grand Slam.
Tennis.body:
Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend won the women's doubles at the US Open to complete a historic career doubles Grand Slam as a pairing. The top seeds came from a set down to beat American wildcards Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery 5-7 6-0 6-2 in New York.

Their triumph at Flushing Meadows means they have now won all four Grand Slam titles, adding to their triumphs at Wimbledon in 2024, the Australian Open in 2025 and this year's French Open.

Tennis.title: US Open: Sky Sports agrees three-year extension to show the US Open until end of 2030
Tennis.summary: US Open: Sky Sports agrees three-year extension to show the US Open until end of 2030 Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Sky has agreed a three-year extension to its US Open deal, ensuring Sky Sports and NOW remains the exclusive home of the tournament in the UK and Ireland until the end of 2030.

As part of the partnership with the United States Tennis Association (USTA), Sky Sports will retain exclusive live coverage of all men's and women's singles, doubles, mixed doubles, juniors and wheelchair competitions throughout the three-week tournament. The agreement was negotiated by the USTA's media rights partner, IMG.

Tennis.title: Bed at 6:45am - US Open semi-finalists fight effects of late-night finishes
Tennis.summary: New York is known as the city that never sleeps. But that comes at a price for US Open stars - including men's semi-finalists Ben Shelton and Alexander Zverev.
Tennis.body:
New York is known as the city that never sleeps - and so it has been at this year's US Open. A number of matches have started late and finished in the early hours, backing up the city's reputation as a playground for the nocturnal.

But when some players - including men's semi-finalists Ben Shelton and Alexander Zverev - are heading to bed as Manhattan commuters are waking up for work, it raises questions about fairness.

Tennis.title: How 9/11 'shattered the guise of safety' for tennis' travelling circus
Tennis.summary: On Friday, the US Open will pause and remember the victims of the 9/11 terror attack that took place 25 years ago.
Tennis.body:
The Arthur Ashe Stadium will glow light blue from dusk until dawn as the US Open marks the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks. American flags will be flown at half-mast as New York remembers the 2,977 people who died when hijackers crashed passenger jets into the Twin Towers in Manhattan on that day in 2001.

That year's US Open had concluded just two days earlier, with Lleyton Hewitt winning the men's singles title. American player James Blake had lost in the second round that year and was in Augusta, Georgia, on Tuesday, 11 September.

Tennis.title: US Open: Elena Rybakina defeats Coco Gauff to silence New York crowd and set up blockbuster final with Aryna Sabalenka
Tennis.summary: US Open: Elena Rybakina defeats Coco Gauff to silence New York crowd and set up blockbuster final with Aryna Sabalenka Sky Sports

American hearts were broken as Elena Rybakina silenced Coco Gauff and the New York crowd to set up a blockbuster US Open final against Aryna Sabalenka, who defeated Jessica Pegula to move a win away from her third straight title at Flushing Meadows.

Rybakina battled back to upset home favourite Gauff 3-6 6-4 6-4 in a fierce semi-final showdown to secure a title showdown with defending champion Sabalenka and stay on course for a third Grand Slam crown.

Tennis.title: US Open chief Craig Tiley tells Sky Sports Tennis he plans on keeping day and night format at Flushing Meadows in 2027
Tennis.summary: US Open chief Craig Tiley tells Sky Sports Tennis he plans on keeping day and night format at Flushing Meadows in 2027 Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
US Open chief Craig Tiley has told Sky Sports Tennis he plans on keeping two matches during the day and two at night at Flushing Meadows in 2027. Tiley, who took the helm as new CEO of USTA earlier this year after leading Tennis Australia since 2013, says he has no plans for any changes to the schedule.

It comes after Ben Shelton's five-set thriller against Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-finals ended at 3:33am local time on Wednesday, leaving few people awake to see the near five-hour marathon reach its finale on one of the sport's biggest stages.

Tennis.title: Rybakina sets up blockbuster Sabalenka final at US Open
Tennis.summary: Soon-to-be world number one Elena Rybakina will face Aryna Sabalenka in a blockbuster US Open final between the tournament's top two seeds.
Tennis.body:
Soon-to-be world number one Elena Rybakina produced a gritty comeback against Coco Gauff to reach the US Open final, in which she will face Aryna Sabalenka in a blockbuster showdown between the tournament's top two seeds.

Rybakina is guaranteed to end Sabalenka's 99-week reign as world number one and will replace the Belarusian at the top when the rankings are updated on Monday. But the Kazakh second seed could rub more salt in Sabalenka's wounds if she can deny the top seed a third successive US Open title in Saturday's showpiece.

Tennis.title: British duo Hewett & Reid into US Open men's wheelchair doubles final
Tennis.summary: British duo Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid come from a set down to reach the final of the men's wheelchair doubles at the US Open.
Tennis.body:
British duo Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid came from a set down to reach the final of the men's wheelchair doubles at the US Open. Hewett and Reid avenged their defeat by the same opponents in last year's final, overcoming Argentina's Gustavo Fernandez and Tokito Oda of Japan in a match tie-break to win 4-6 6-3 10-7.

The pair are bidding for a sixth US Open doubles title together as a partnership, having won five in a row between 2017 and 2021. They will face Spain's Martin de la Puente and Ruben Spaargaren of the Netherlands in the final.

Tennis.title: US Open: Tennis remembers 9/11 25 years on
Tennis.summary: New York native and former top 5 player James Blake shares his memories of September 11
Tennis.body: Today the city of New York marks the 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks which saw two hijacked passenger jets flown into the Twin Towers of the World Trade Centre. The US Open of 2001 had finished two days prior to the attacks with Venus Williams and Leyton Hewitt winning the singles titles. There had been plans for a photoshoot for Hewitt and the trophy to take place at the World Trade Centre the day after the tournament - before being moved to Grand Central station. Russell Fuller has been speaking to James Blake - a former top 5 player - who was born in New York and played in the 2001 edition of the tournament about how sport played a role in America's healing process and how life changed for those who lived in the city in the wake of the atrocity.

Tennis.body:
Reunited three-time US Open men's doubles champions Joe Salisbury and Rajeev Ram knocked out last year's winners Marcel Granollers and Horacio Zeballos to reach the semi-finals.

Tennis.title: US Open: Alexander Zverev passes Botic van de ​Zandschulp test to set up semi-final date with Karen Khachanov
Tennis.summary: US Open: Alexander Zverev passes Botic van de ​Zandschulp test to set up semi-final date with Karen Khachanov Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Alexander Zverev took another big step towards a second Grand Slam title by beating Dutchman Botic van de Zandschulp 6-2 7-5 6-1 to reach the US Open semi-finals. The 29-year-old French Open champion and Wimbledon runner-up got off to a slow start in his campaign at Flushing Meadows but has steadily found his range.

Zverev played five-set matches in each of the first two matches, but he has won his last three in straight sets and is the only man to reach all four Grand Slam semi-finals this year.

Tennis.summary: Coco Gauff saves two match points to beat Mirra Andreeva and set up a US Open semi-final against incoming world number one Elena Rybakina.
Tennis.body:
Coco Gauff saved two match points as she fought from a set down to beat Mirra Andreeva and set up a US Open semi-final against incoming world number one Elena Rybakina. Blown away in a 26-minute opening set, fourth seed Gauff was twice pegged back from a break up in a scrappy second set before coming through a 16-point tie-break to force a decider.

Roared on by a partisan crowd, the American's resilience proved the difference in what became a mental battle as she closed out a 2-6 7-6 (9-7) 6-2 win – a performance she said was inspired by compatriot Frances Tiafoe's comeback victory over Alex Michelsen on Tuesday night.

Tennis.title: Hewett and Reid into last eight of US Open singles
Tennis.summary: British duo Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid win their respective first-round matches in the men's wheelchair singles at the US Open.
Tennis.body:
British duo Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid both reached the men's wheelchair singles quarter-finals at the US Open on Wednesday. Hewett, the number two seed and a four-time winner in New York, dropped only two games in a 6-0 6-2 victory against Spain's Daniel Caverzaschi and will face American Casey Ratzlaff for a place in the semi-finals.

Reid's match against Frenchman Stephane Houdet was a much closer contest, with the Scot eventually winning 6-3 5-7 6-2 in two hours and 13 minutes. Up next for Reid is the defending champion and top seed Tokito Oda of Japan, who has won the past six Grand Slam singles titles.

Tennis.title: US Open: 3.33am local time and another early-morning finish as Ben Shelton beat Carlos Alcaraz, so does something have to change?
Tennis.summary: US Open: 3.33am local time and another early-morning finish as Ben Shelton beat Carlos Alcaraz, so does something have to change? Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
US Open: 3.33am local time and another early-morning finish as Ben Shelton beat Carlos Alcaraz, so does something have to change? The clock ticked to 3.33am local time in New York City when Ben Shelton beat Carlos Alcaraz with a clean ace to the delight of thousands of delirious tennis fans still inside Arthur Ashe Stadium, but does something have to be done to stop these early-morning finishes?

Three long matches earlier on Tuesday meant Alcaraz and Shelton did not step on to court until gone 11pm. The US Open craves its night matches and players love the energy the fans provide - even when a number of matches have already gone past 2am this year.

Tennis.title: 'Just a number'
Tennis.summary: Elena Rybakina becomes the new women's world number one after reaching the US Open semi-finals, ending Aryna Sabalenka's 99-week reign at the top of the rankings.
Tennis.body:
After 99 weeks, there will be a new women's world number one - and it will be Elena Rybakina. Rybakina confirmed she will replace Aryna Sabalenka at the top of the world rankings on Monday with her US Open quarter-final victory over China's Zheng Qinwen.

Despite losing a set for the first time in the tournament, Rybakina fought back and saved a break point in the deciding set to complete a 3-6 6-1 6-4 win. She is the first Kazakhstani man or woman to reach the top of the singles standings.

The US Open is fully underway, and tennis fans will notice that one star player is noticeably missing: Emma Raducanu. It’s a tournament that has special significance for the British player. Tennis.title: Osaka makes passionate defence of on-court outfits
Tennis.summary: Naomi Osaka says any criticism she receives for her outfits is "worth it" if it means "the people after me have an easier path".
Tennis.body:
Naomi Osaka says any criticism she receives for her extravagant outfits is "worth it" if it means "the people after me have an easier path". The 28-year-old is renowned for her eye-catching on-court attire, which included a hooded white gown for her first-round win against Anastasia Zakharova at the US Open.

Underneath was an all-black basketball-style kit in which Osaka played, while she also had her hair braided and wore a headband in a tribute to former NBA star Allen Iverson, who she called a "trailblazer" as "he's kind of like done a lot in fashion, whether it's on purpose or not".

Tennis.title: More than the Score
Tennis.summary: Crowd behaviour has been in the spotlight at the US Open
Tennis.body: This year, the US Open gave accreditation to nearly 100 social media influencers and content creators. The tournament sees them as crucial to helping promote tennis to younger audiences - but they've also been accused of disrupting matches. Jessica Pegula and Naomi Osaka are among the players who have complained about crowd behaviour at Flushing Meadows, with umpires having to pause some matches due to excess noise and bright lights in the stands. But do influencers deserve this criticism - and what are content creators and tennis gaining from each other? Rachel Stuhlmann, one of the world's leading tennis influencers, tells More than the Score's Delyth Lloyd how she's built her career over the past decade, and the day-to-day realities of creating content at the world's biggest tournaments. Delyth's also joined by Sara Gordano from the sports business site Sportico, who explains tennis's relationship with the creator economy - and why the US Open's "party" atmosphere gives it a very different character from other Grand Slams. Tennis.title: US Open: Is Zheng Qinwen going to give us another Emma Raducanu moment in New York?
Tennis.summary: US Open: Is Zheng Qinwen going to give us another Emma Raducanu moment in New York? thenationalnews.com
Tennis.body:
Five years ago at the US Open, Emma Raducanu, then ranked 150th in the world, pulled off a miracle and became the first qualifier in tennis history to win a Grand Slam title. In June this year, Maja Chwalinska, ranked 114th, was one victory away from replicating that feat as she stormed to the French Open final as a qualifier. She ultimately lost the title match to Mirra Andreeva.

Zheng broke down in tears during her post-match press conference that day at Roland Garros. She had won just seven matches in the six events she had contested since returning to the tour in February. She was searching for a spark to ignite the competitive fire within her that had been missing throughout her comeback thus far.

Tennis.title: US Open 2026: Aryna Sabalenka edges into semi-finals with three-set win over Linda Noskova
Tennis.summary: US Open 2026: Aryna Sabalenka edges into semi-finals with three-set win over Linda Noskova Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Aryna Sabalenka maintained her hopes of a third successive US Open title with a battling three-set win over Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in an absorbing quarter-final - a result that retains her status as world No 1 for at least one more day.

The 28-year-old beat Noskova 7-6 (7-1) 3-6 7-6 (10-7), coming through two tie-breaks - and a 4-2 deficit in the final set - as she sealed victory with a second-serve ace to set up a meeting with Jessica Pegula.

Tennis.title: Tiafoe consoles tearful Michelsen after remarkable comeback
Tennis.summary: Frances Tiafoe comes from two sets and a break down to beat Alex Michelsen in a thrilling comeback to reach the US Open semi-finals.
Tennis.body:
Frances Tiafoe came from two sets and a break down to beat fellow American Alex Michelsen in a thrilling comeback to reach the US Open semi-finals. Eleventh seed Tiafoe was outplayed by world number 46 Michelsen for the first half of the match, but battled back from 5-3 down in the third set to ignite a remarkable turnaround.

In a final set of multiple breaks and swings of momentum, Tiafoe triumphed in the 10-point tie-break to win 5-7 3-6 7-5 6-3 7-6 (10-6). Victory means 28-year-old Tiafoe reaches his third US Open semi-final in five years, where he will play defending champion Carlos Alcaraz or American eighth seed Ben Shelton.

Tennis.summary: Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid start their bid for a sixth wheelchair doubles title at the US Open with a dominant victory in New York.

Tennis.title: Sabalenka thought title defence was over before US Open fightback
Tennis.summary: Aryna Sabalenka battles back to beat sixth seed Linda Noskova in three sets and advance to the semi-finals.
Tennis.body:
Aryna Sabalenka thought she had lost her US Open crown before battling back to beat Linda Noskova in three sets and advance to the semi-finals. Taken to a deciding set for the first time in this year's tournament, the two-time defending champion trailed 4-2 in the third set and later 2-0 in the tie-break before recovering to close out the win in a little under two and a half hours.

It was the 28-year-old's 19th consecutive win at the tournament, having not tasted defeat since the 2023 final, while she becomes the first woman since Serena Williams in 2016 to reach six successive semi-finals at Flushing Meadows.

Tennis.title: From match point to US Open exit
Tennis.summary: France's Arthur Gea held match point to become the first lucky loser to reach a Grand Slam quarter-final - three hours later he was out of the US Open.
Tennis.body:
France's Arthur Gea was one point away from being the first lucky loser to reach a Grand Slam quarter-final - but three hours later he was out of the US Open. Gea, 21, was unable to convert a match point in a third-set tie-break against Dutch opponent Botic van de Zandschulp, then could not serve out victory in the fourth set of a gruelling fourth-round contest.

Van de Zandschulp took full advantage to escape from the jaws of defeat, going on to secure a 3-6 6-7 (0-7) 7-6 (9-7) 7-6 (7-3) 6-4 win after five hours and 13 minutes - the fourth longest match on record at Flushing Meadows.

Tennis.title: Gauff's statement win completes stacked US Open last eight
Tennis.summary: Coco Gauff powers past teenage star Iva Jovic as the top six seeds reach the US Open women's quarter-finals for the first time in 28 years.
Tennis.body:
It was not so long ago that Coco Gauff was the teenage sensation looking to cause an upset at the US Open. Now, at the grand old age of 22, she is the Grand Slam champion and leading WTA Tour star who drew on her experience to deal with talented 18-year-old Iva Jovic at Flushing Meadows.

Fourth seed Gauff found her finest level of the fortnight to beat fellow American Jovic in a 6-1 6-4 win and secure her place in the quarter-finals. Gauff's comfortable progress ensured the top six seeds have reached the US Open women's last eight for the first time since 1998, further illustrating the strength in depth at the top of the WTA Tour.

But the world No. 70 shared an exciting video of herself hitting some serves on Monday, more than 3,000 miles away from Flushing Meadows.

Tennis.title: 'We're not robots'
Tennis.summary: The chaotic nature of the men's draw has been a sharp contrast to the relative calm of the women's - but anyone can still win the US Open titles.
Tennis.body:
Talent, athleticism and commitment are not nearly enough to become a Grand Slam singles champion. Possessing the confidence that you can beat anyone on the biggest stage - where the eyes of the world are fixed on you and there is no place to hide - is arguably the most important characteristic a player can have.

Unwavering belief. Or, as former US Open runner-up Taylor Fritz describes it, delusion. Fritz is one of the current crop of leading men yet to get his hands on one of the sport's major prizes. The world number 10 is also one of the guys who has blown what looked like a golden opportunity to win this year's US Open.

"I really enjoyed it and I think that's something that I want to take forward in all my matches and really embrace this grass-court season."

Tennis.summary: Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka emulates Serena Williams by overcoming Taylor Townsend to reach a sixth straight US Open quarter-final.
Tennis.body:
Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka emulated Serena Williams as she eventually overpowered American Taylor Townsend to reach a sixth straight US Open quarter-final. A topsy-turvy contest featured 10 breaks of serve, but Sabalenka recovered from 3-1 down in the second serve to seal a 6-4 6-3 victory with a fifth consecutive game.

It was the Belarusian's 18th consecutive win at the tournament, extending her three-year unbeaten streak following back-to-back triumphs in 2024 and 2025. Sabalenka, 28, is the first woman to reach six consecutive singles quarter-finals at Flushing Meadows since American great Williams in 2016.

Tennis.summary: Zheng Qinwen fights back from 5-0 down in the deciding set and stares down match point to stun American 22nd seed Madison Keys.
Tennis.body:
Zheng Qinwen described her US Open third-round comeback win over Madison Keys as a "very dramatic match" - but that is somewhat of an understatement. The Olympic champion, who had to come through qualifying to reach the main draw, found herself 5-0 and match point down in the third set against Keys.

Golf.title: The Solheim Cup venue isn't a 'club' or 'course.' Here's why
Golf.summary: Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands, host of the 2026 Solheim Cup, is a high-end property and a smartly cultivated brand. The post The Solheim Cup venue isn’t a ‘club’ or ‘course.’ Here’s why appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
What’s in a name? At this week’s Solheim Cup in the Netherlands, the question gives us plenty to unpack. The host venue is Bernardus Golf, a name that’s notable for what’s not in it. No mention of “club.” No reference to “course.”

Robert van der Wallen, the Dutch entrepreneur who developed Bernardus, set out to create an upscale members’ enclave without the starchy trappings of a country club. He wanted the property to feel exclusive. He didn’t want it to be off limits. So he omitted “club,” with its closed-circle connotations. And he left out “course,” with its utilitarian implications. What remained — Bernardus Golf — has the ring of a lifestyle brand, an experience anyone can access.

Golf.body:
Brendon de Jonge enjoyed a lengthy PGA Tour career that encompassed 317 starts. While he never notched a victory, de Jonge did post 10 top-5s, 28 top-10s and 68 top-25 finishes between 2007 and 2018. The 46-year-old is now working in broadcast media as an on-air analyst and radio host.

On this week’s episode of Subpar, de Jonge joined hosts Colt Knost and Drew Stoltz to reflect on his some of his career highlights, including his experience on the 2013 Presidents Cup team, where he was paired with Ernie Els and tasked with taking on Tiger Woods and Matt Kuchar in Saturday afternoon’s foursomes matches.

Golf.title: The Harbor Course at Wild Dunes is teeming with history and lowcountry charm
Golf.summary: Explore Wild Dunes’ newly renovated Harbor Course, featuring $8 million in upgrades, lowcountry scenery and unexpected historic significance. The post The Harbor Course at Wild Dunes is teeming with history and lowcountry charm appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Tucked away on Isle of Palms is Wild Dunes, a lowcountry South Carolina golf retreat that seems to have it all: towering live oaks draped in Spanish moss, palmettos that frame the greens, marshland stretching along nearby fairways and the glittering Atlantic just beyond the dunes.

It’s the kind of coastal scene that makes you slow down so much that you almost forget you’re supposed to be keeping score. The Harbor Course, however, has a way of bringing you back to the task at hand.

Golf.body:
A dominating performance from Americans Alison Lee and Lauren Coughlin was the only thing that stood between the Europeans and an early morning foursomes sweep on Saturday at the Solheim Cup.

Europe won the first three matches of Day 2 at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands to take a 7-5 lead. “We don’t like being down, but look, I think this afternoon is really important,” said U.S. captain Angela Stanford. “It’s going to be the toughest session because it’s probably the most fans we have seen out here. They’re getting rowdy. So this is going to be a really tough afternoon. And I told them it’s going to be tough. So hopefully they’re up for it.”

Golf.title: How this new putting 'toolkit' can make you better on the greens
Golf.summary: The Trigon Toolkit from Short Game Gains features four different tools that can help you improve your alignment, start line and more. The post How this new putting ‘toolkit’ can make you better on the greens appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When it comes to putting practice, I’ve always found that a little additional structure can make a significant difference. Using training aids or tools that provide feedback on setup keys and other important details gives my practice more purpose — and ultimately helps me become a more reliable putter under pressure.

That’s why I was interested in trying the Trigon Toolkit from Short Game Gains. I’ve been using their steel putting mirror for the past year or so, and it has become a regular part of my practice routine. The new Trigon Toolkit builds on that same idea by combining several simple putting tools to address different aspects of putting.

Golf.title: Want to hit wedges that spin? Try this simple tee drill
Golf.summary: Top 100 Teacher John Scott Rattan is often asked how to hit chips that spin. Here, he explains how to practice the shot with a simple drill. The post Want to hit wedges that spin? Try this simple tee drill appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One of the most common questions I get is how to hit a wedge that sucks back on the green. You know, the one that bounces past the hole, stops and spins back close to the pin. In reality, it’s a pretty simple shot to hit. Most techniques in the golf swing work in pairs, and flighted scoring clubs are no different. If we can manage the clubface and loft early in the swing, impact becomes a by-product.

One of the best ways to practice this is by placing a golf tee in your lead hand between your middle and ring fingers, all the way at the base. Make your backswing and feel like you’re twisting the tee behind you in transition.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy played his slowest-ever round. Then came different kind of test
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy's Irish Open defense got off to a slow start. His opening round took six hours, and Friday brought more challenges. The post Rory McIlroy played his slowest-ever round. Then came different kind of test appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
“I can’t recall a round of golf that has taken that long before. We’ve had some rounds that are five-and-a-half or five-and-three-quarter hours, but six hours is a first for me.”

McIlroy wasn’t being hyperbolic. He and his playing partners, Robert MacIntyre and Brooks Koepka, had started their round at Doonbeg, on Ireland’s southwest coast, at 1:35 p.m. local time. Their group’s final putt dropped at 7:41, meaning their round clocked in at a cool 6 hours and 6 minutes, or roughly the same time it takes to fly from New York to Dublin.

Golf.body:
Fred Couples may be the coolest man in golf. And at this week’s Sanford International, he added to that lore. At a Wednesday evening sponsor outing ahead of the event, there was a closest-to-the pin shootout from just off the green. With daylight fading over the clubhouse, Couples stepped up to his pitch and, with as smooth an action as ever, lofted his ball onto the green. As the ball rolled toward the hole, Couples turned around and started interacting with those around him.

Golf.title: GOLF Magazine announces 2026 World Golf Teachers Hall of Fame inductees
Golf.summary: The 2026 World Golf Teachers Hall of Fame inductees include Todd Anderson, Martin Hall, Ted Sheftic and the late Dana Rader. The post GOLF Magazine announces 2026 World Golf Teachers Hall of Fame inductees appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
GOLF Magazine this week announced its 2026 class for the World Golf Teachers Hall of Fame. The inductees include Todd Anderson, Martin Hall, Ted Sheftic and the late Dana Rader.

These inductees will be honored at the 2026 GOLF Top 100 Teachers Summit, which will take place Nov. 1-4 at the Omni La Costa Resort & Spa in Carlsbad, Calif. “Each of the instructors we have chosen to enter the World Golf Teachers Hall of Fame this year has earned the distinction in their own unique way,” said Hoyt McGarity, CEO and President of 8AM Golf, the parent company of GOLF Magazine and GOLF.com. “The groundbreaking efforts and longevity of the careers of Todd, Martin, Ted, and Dana are something to behold and it’s an honor to recognize each of them for their extraordinary contributions.”

Golf.title: Ciganda's late sparkle lifts Europe on dramatic opening day of Solheim Cup
Golf.summary: Carlota Ciganda steals the show after Europe's top pairing of Charley Hull and Lottie Woad fail to ignite on day one of the Solheim Cup against the United States.
Golf.body:
Carlota Ciganda once again stole the show after Europe's top pairing of Charley Hull and Lottie Woad failed to ignite against the USA on the opening day of the Solheim Cup. The 36-year-old Spaniard - the oldest player competing this weekend - let out a roar after holing a 15-foot putt to earn Europe an unlikely half point in the final fourball match of the day and ensure honours are even at 4-4.

Ciganda's celebration evoked memories of the nerve-shredding finale at Finca Cortesin in 2023, when her putt allowed Europe to retain the trophy with a 14-14 tie. And once again Nelly Korda, beaten by Ciganda in Spain three years ago, was on the receiving end.

Golf.body:
Eight matches played. Four points for the United States. Four points for the Europeans. If there’s anything we learned after Friday’s first-day play at the Solheim Cup, it’s that the next two days should be good at Bernardus Golf course in the Netherlands.

The biggest drama on Friday was saved for the very end. On the par-4 18, the European duo of Carlota Ciganda and Julia Lopez Ramirez and Americans Nelly Korda and Lauren Coughlin were all square in their four-ball match — and Ciganda’s clubface on the tee wasn’t square. She went right. On her second shot, she played up the adjacent first hole. From right of the green with her third shot, she pitched to 10 feet. Ahead of her, the Americans were in with a par, and Lopez Ramirez bogeyed.

Golf.title: The Solheim Cup, now 20 editions old, owes much to its namesake
Golf.summary: You might have heard the Ryder Cup is named for British seed merchant Samuel Ryder. The Solheim Cup’s origin story is less well known. The post The Solheim Cup, now 20 editions old, owes much to its namesake appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Everyone seems to know that the Ryder Cup is named for — altogether now — the British seed merchant Samuel Ryder, who donated the trophy. But how many people know that the Solheim Cup is named for a transplanted Norwegian named Karsten Solheim, who started making a pinging putter in a garage in Phoenix that eventually became an innovative club-manufacturing empire known throughout golfdom as Ping, a division of Karsten Manufacturing?

“We gave them three options for the name of the event,” John Solheim, one of Karsten’s sons, now in his early 80s, said the other day. His them was the organizing bodies that put on the Solheim Cup, the LPGA and the LET, the Ladies’ European Tour. “Solheim Cup, Karsten Cup or Ping Cup. I’m glad they went with Solheim.”

Golf.summary: Matt Thurmond of ASU men's golf has built a career on building good men first and Tour stars second. The challenges of that may surprise you. The post How great college players become great pros, according to a top college coach appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Every time I walk the range at a big amateur event or spend time testing with elite college kids, I see the same thing: launch monitor numbers that would make half the guys in the top 50 in the world blush.

Ball speed that jumps off the face. Efficiency numbers through the roof. Perfect wedge gaps. To the untrained eye, the conclusion is simple: How is this kid not walking directly onto the PGA Tour tomorrow?

Golf.title: These versatile pieces of apparel made packing for my golf trip a breeze
Golf.summary: When a golf trip called for fashionable, functional pieces that easily transitioned from on course to off, TravisMathew came to the rescue. The post These versatile pieces of apparel made packing for my golf trip a breeze appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Readers of this space may recall that I am a staunch proponent of carry-on luggage. I have come to believe, no matter the length of your trip, if it involves air travel, traveling with a carry-on is a non-negotiable. I managed to do it on a two-week international trip for the last two years, which helped me feel empowered to limit myself to a carry-on for every subsequent trip since, regardless of the destination.

That is, until I had a golf trip on the horizon. Uh oh. The trip was only three days, but the variety of outfits required — travel apparel, on- and off-course options, post-golf attire, and multiple pairs of shoes, of course — had me doubting myself. How could a carry-on provide all of the packing space I needed? The solution was obvious: I needed to bring clothes that work just as well on the course as they do off. But that strategy brought another problem to the surface: Multi-functional golf apparel that functions well on the course and looks suitable off it is notoriously hard to find — especially for women.

Golf.title: LIV Golf Loses a Golf State
Golf.summary: LIV Golf Loses a Golf State VideoAge International
Golf.body:
The golf league LIV Golf, founded to challenge the American PGA Tour, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in New Jersey, with up to $1 billion in liabilities, after its primary backer, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), pulled its funding four years after LIV was founded. The Gulf state had poured some $5 billion into the LIV Golf venture.

Reportedly, the league’s top seven creditors are LIV players themselves. However, PIF is providing a $49.6 million loan to fund the bankruptcy proceedings, while LIV is seeking $300 million in additional investment to keep the golf league going.

Golf.summary: Greg Norman reveals his biggest LIV Golf regret after league’s bankruptcy filing Golfmagic
Golf.body:
Greg Norman has admitted LIV Golf got one of its biggest strategic decisions wrong from the outset, while insisting he never intended to destroy the PGA Tour. The former LIV CEO and commissioner offered his most detailed assessment yet of the controversial Saudi-backed league in an interview with Flushing It’s Tom Hobbs, just days after LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.

Norman, who left his leadership role two years ago with Scott O’Neil taking over, remains adamant that his objective was never to bring down the PGA Tour. “I never wanted to destroy the PGA Tour,” Norman told Hobbs, while arguing that LIV was unfairly judged during the bitter split in professional golf.

Golf.title: Mickelson Is Unnamed Player-Shareholder in LIV Golf Filing
Golf.summary: Mickelson Is Unnamed Player-Shareholder in LIV Golf Filing Sportico.com
Golf.body:
Phil Mickelson owned a 0.23% stake in LIV Golf at the time of its bankruptcy filings, according to a person familiar with the matter. On Tuesday, LIV Golf submitted a 128-page document to tee off its Chapter 11 proceedings in the District of New Jersey, outlining financial details such as the cap table of the tour. LIV Golf had issued 98.48% of its common ownership to the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, 1.05% to Performance54 Group Limited, an entity controlled by PIF, and 0.23% to former CEO Greg Norman. The document also noted a 0.23% stake held by a “current player.”

The identity of the unnamed golfer is Mickelson, said the person, who was granted anonymity because the matter is private. LIV Golf declined to comment. A representative for Mickelson did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

Golf.title: The best way to learn how to change trajectories with your wedges
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Joey Wuertemberger explains how to teach yourself to hit a lower, more penetrating wedge shot. The post The best way to learn how to change trajectories with your wedges appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Great wedge players don’t just know how far their wedges go. They know how to control how the ball gets there. They do this by changing trajectories, which gives them another way to manage distance, spin and how the ball reacts when it lands.

A big part of that control comes from understanding how much loft you deliver to the ball at impact. If you add loft, the ball tends to launch higher. If you can deliver less loft while maintaining a quality strike, you can produce a lower, more penetrating flight.

Golf.title: This 1 piece of swing data separates low- and high-handicap golfers
Golf.summary: Looking at pelvis sway numbers at the top of the backswing can give a great look at the difference between good and bad golfers. The post This 1 piece of swing data separates low- and high-handicap golfers appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:

But there’s one data point that nearly always differentiates good and bad golfers — and you don’t even need to see a golfer’s full swing to know where he or she falls on this spectrum.

Golf.summary: The decline of LIV Golf: From April’s shocking funding loss to September’s bankruptcy The New York Times
Golf.body:
One of professional golf’s more turbulent eras reached a new milestone on Tuesday, when LIV Golf filed for bankruptcy and announced plans to restructure ahead of its 2027 season.

LIV’s decision comes after four years of battles across links, courtrooms and financial filings over how the Saudi-backed upstart could function in a sport long dominated by the PGA Tour. But speculation about the promotion’s financial health dates to its first emergence, and despite the public optimism of LIV officials, its future remains unclear.

Golf.title: Mizuno adds to M.Craft X line with new zero-torque neck putter
Golf.summary: Mizuno is expanding its modular M.Craft X putter line with a new zero-torque neck option as well as two new head shapes. The post Mizuno adds to M.Craft X line with new zero-torque neck putter appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Mizuno’s new putter doesn’t look low-torque, and it doesn’t balance like a typical one either. The newest neck option to the modular Mizuno M.Craft X putter line, the M.Craft X Z, orients the shaft directly through the CG of the putter, ensuring the putter balances exactly where you hold it instead of wanting to return to toe-up. This creates what the company calls a truly zero-torque design.

“This was all about putting zero bias in it,” Mizuno director of golf Chris Voshall told GOLF. “So our goal on all of these is to fire the shaft axis directly through the CG. So a little bit different than the lie angle balanced or the square-to-square, like how they’re executing on a zero-torque or a low-torque design. So we call it infinite toe hang. It’ll hang wherever you put it.

Today’s best golf shoes blend athletic comfort with the stability and traction needed to swing confidently. This latest group features five compelling new options from FootJoy, Sun Day Red, Nike, Payntr and TRUE Linkswear. Some emphasize all-day walking comfort, while others focus on ground connection, lateral support and aggressive grip.

A firm EVA forefoot and nylon spring plate add stability and energy return, while a StratoFOAM heel pad, padded ankle collar and OrthoLite FitBed help keep the shoe comfortable during walking rounds. It is also backed by a two-year waterproof warranty.

Golf.title: How history points to another Solheim Cup thriller
Golf.summary: With no more than one point separating the teams at the past three Solheim Cups played in Europe there is every reason to expect that this week's contest will be just as exciting, writes Iain Carter.
Golf.body:
Recent history suggests this week's Solheim Cup will be another epic clash to follow hot on the heels of Great Britain and Ireland's dramatic victory over the United States in the Walker Cup.

The extraordinary climax at Lahinch last Sunday, where GB&I won with the last putt of the match, evoked memories of the past three Solheim Cups staged in Europe. Three years ago in Spain the contest ended in a dramatic 14-14 tie to allow a delirious European team to hold on to the trophy, having initially wrestled it from American hands with a single-point victory at Gleneagles in 2019.

Golf.title: “The power battle for golf, and its biggest players, might not be over just yet” | Media Centre
Golf.summary: “The power battle for golf, and its biggest players, might not be over just yet” | Media Centre Loughborough University
Golf.body:
“Five years on from LIV’s inception, golf’s power battle appears to have swung back in favour of the PGA. However, it may feel like victory but at a cost. The PGA have had to function without some of the biggest names in the sport for the last few years and has had to bolster their prize money as a result, even going so far as to create a for-profit business model that offers the players future equity stakes in the company.

“Viewed through this lens, the entry of LIV Golf, while controversial, did act as a catalyst for both innovation and defensive consolidation within the sport. The response from the PGA Tour was immediate and material, most notably through significant increases in prize money and the acceleration of strategic alignment with the DP World Tour. The introduction of PGA Tour cards for the top performers in the Race to Dubai was a clear signal of intent: to strengthen institutional ties and reinforce the traditional ecosystem in the face of external disruption.

Golf.title: This U.S. star has been sick. At Solheim Cup, she’ll need to find strength
Golf.summary: U.S. star Angel Yin is playing in the Solheim Cup in the Netherlands after a two-month break from competition for a stomach illness. The post This U.S. star has been sick. At Solheim Cup, she’ll need to find strength appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The first signs that Angel Yin was not well came at the KPMG Women’s PGA Championship in Minnesota in late June. Yin, who was then ranked 16th in the world, opened with a solid one-under 71 — then checked herself into a hospital, complaining of stomach pain. The next day, Yin was on the back on the course, at shin-kicking Hazeltine National, where she dug deep and posted another 71 to make the cut by two. But by Saturday morning, Yin, who is 27, was back in the hospital with no hope of playing the third round. She was hospitalized for another six days before flying home to Florida. She would have weeks more of gastrointestinal challenges ahead of her.

Over the next two months, Yin was unable to return to competition and limited her diet to the likes of rice, boiled chicken and cooked vegetables, she told Golfweek’s Beth Ann Nichols. Yin wasn’t trying to lose weight but she did: 35 pounds in all. In late August, she returned to the LPGA, at the FM Championship at TPC Boston. It did not go well, at least not in terms of the numbers on her scorecards: 81-76. More worrying still, the Solheim Cup, for which Yin had qualified months earlier, was less than two weeks away.

Golf.title: How to put spin on your pitch shots (the right way!), according to a top teacher
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Joey Wuertemberger explains that proper technique to put spin on your pitch shots around the green. The post How to put spin on your pitch shots (the right way!), according to a top teacher appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One of the biggest misconceptions in wedge play is that you have to do something special with your hands to make the ball check. Players try to cut across it, flip the clubhead under the ball or add excessive loft. What those types of players fail to understand is that spin isn’t a trick or gimmick. It’s simply the result of creating the right conditions between the clubface and the ball at impact.

Clean contact, clean grooves, enough speed and the proper amount of loft create friction. And friction is what allows the ball to grab the face, launch with control and spin when it hits the green.

Golf.title: The lessons of LIV Golf’s failure
Golf.summary: The lessons of LIV Golf’s failure Financial Times
Golf.body:
Roula Khalaf, Editor of the FT, selects her favourite stories in this weekly newsletter. Four years ago, LIV Golf promised “golf, but louder”. Protracted 72-hole tournaments would be swapped for higher-octane 54-hole team events with shotgun starts — simultaneous tee-offs at different holes — blaring music and huge payouts for players. Backed by $5bn-plus of investment from Saudi Arabia, it was an attempt to disrupt the sedate world of golf and build soft power for Riyadh. After the Saudi Public Investment Fund said in April it would pull funding, LIV Golf filed for bankruptcy protection this week. It hopes to launch a “LIV 2.0” backed by buyout firm BC Partners. But LIV 1.0 is over, along with Saudi hopes of building a rival power centre in golf — though not Riyadh’s newfound clout in many other sports.

LIV Golf was the flagship of a broader Saudi sports investment strategy. This was often justifiably portrayed as an exercise in “sportswashing” the kingdom’s record of human rights abuses. But there was something more to the investment. It was another way to diversify the economy away from oil, and hosting sports events could help make the kingdom more attractive to tourists. And it was intended to get young Saudis off their couches — but involved in pursuits not connected to politics.

Golf.title: McIlroy warns tours have ‘decisions to make’ as LIV Golf exodus edges closer
Golf.summary: McIlroy warns tours have ‘decisions to make’ as LIV Golf exodus edges closer The Guardian
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy believes traditional tours will soon have “decisions to make” as a player exodus from LIV Golf edges closer. LIV filing for bankruptcy in the United States on Tuesday means its deals with several high-profile golfers will soon be invalid, leaving them free to negotiate a route back to the PGA and DP World Tours. When asked whether remaining with LIV in its planned, far-less lucrative form would hold appeal, McIlroy was characteristically candid. “I’m not in their shoes but LIV at the start looked a lot more attractive than what LIV 2.0 might be from a financial standpoint,” said the Masters champion.

The Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing – stating around $45m (£33.2m) is owed to players – represented LIV’s latest step in rebooting the business due to the removal of funding from Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF). Sources familiar with the situation insist contracts have not yet been breached. Terms in place with star names are now unaffordable for LIV. Contracts will inevitably either be renegotiated or cancelled.

Golf.title: What next for LIV Golf's star players, and its fight for survival?
Golf.summary: Golf's main tours are expecting a lot of interest in rejoining from LIV golfers – but the path back might not be so easy.
Golf.body:
The DP World Tour has said it has had a "high volume" of interest from LIV Golf players and is exploring ways to accommodate those who leave the breakaway league. It comes as LIV Golf filed for bankruptcy protection in the US on Tuesday, as it attempts to restructure for a "new era" next year.

LIV owes at least $45m (£33m) to 14 current and former players. Its golfers, including star names like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm, can now opt to leave, rather than being obliged to see out their contracts in LIV 2.0 which is aiming to launch next year.

Golf.title: Troubled league LIV Golf files for bankruptcy protection in US
Golf.summary: Troubled league LIV Golf files for bankruptcy protection in US Al Jazeera
Golf.body:
Less than five years after it held its first event and created a schism in professional golf, LIV Golf has filed for bankruptcy protection in New Jersey, United States. The Chapter 11 bankruptcy, or reorganisation bankruptcy, filed on Tuesday, allows the debtor to remain in possession and operate its business, according to US Courts.

The move offers a rare window into the league’s financial state, with LIV Golf owing between $500m and $1bn in estimated liabilities to at least 1,000 creditors, including star players like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm.

Golf.title: LIV Golf files for bankruptcy: What we know
Golf.summary: LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy Tuesday, confirming what was long-rumored: it owes a lot of money and plans to restructure. The post LIV Golf files for bankruptcy: What we know appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Following months of rumors, lawsuits and financial unease, LIV Golf has officially filed for bankruptcy. The rival golf league that took on the status quo in pro golf has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in New Jersey, formally marking some end to, as Jon Rahm called it Tuesday morning, LIV Golf 1.0. Chapter 11 is best understood as a corporate restructuring mechanism with intent to continue.

The filing arrived shortly after 4 p.m. ET and includes some information not previously released, like money owed to players and various vendors that have recently taken LIV to court for unpaid services. Also Tuesday, we had confirmation of LIV’s “lead investor” that CEO Scott O’Neil first mentioned a month ago; O’Neil also wrote a letter to fans about LIV’s next phase.

Golf.title: 'False' Charley Hull story shut down by her Solheim Cup captains
Golf.summary: Charley Hull's Solheim Cup captains cleared up the reason for her late arrival to a Tuesday-morning practice round in the Netherlands. The post ‘False’ Charley Hull story shut down by her Solheim Cup captains appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Why was Charley Hull, Team Europe’s biggest star, late for her Tuesday-morning practice round at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands? The query was directed at Europe’s captain, Anna Nordqvist, and her three lieutenants, Caroline Hedwall, Mel Reid and Anne van Dam, at their captain’s press conference.

Reid did, because, as she saw it, she had some rumors to quash. “This could be a full story,” Reid began. “Charley Hull was the first one to bed last night at 8 o’clock and first one on the bus this morning. She doesn’t even drink, so that’s a completely false story it’s been misquoted. She was late to the tee because I was responsible for her, so I’ll take a little bit of responsibility to that. But she just thought her tee time was a little bit later, and trying to drag Charley Hull off a driving range is a feat in any tournament, especially a Solheim. So yeah it’s a completely false story.”

Golf.body:
We know where Jon Rahm is playing this week. But where the two-time major champion and LIV Golf pro will tee it up next year is an open question. Rahm is in Ireland this week to compete in the 2026 Amgen Irish Open, a DP World Tour event that’s drawing an impressive field from LIV and PGA Tour ranks, including Rory McIlroy.

LIV Golf’s 2026 season, though, is over after coming to an abrupt and early end at LIV Indianapolis last month, and the league’s future is uncertain. Following the Saudi Public Investment Fund’s decision to pull funding, the league is hoping to create a new-look LIV Golf 2.0 for next season.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: I made an ace — with my playing partner's club! Is it legal?
Golf.summary: If you make a hole-in-one with another player's club, does it count? Rules Guy has the answer — and it might surprise you. The post Rules Guy: I made an ace — with my playing partner’s club! Is it legal? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’’e got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. A friendly four-ball match. We reach a par-3, and my buddy looks to pull his 6-iron only to realize he left it on a prior hole. Another player offered up his 6 and, sure enough, my pal jars his first-ever ace. We counted it…but I’m thinking he’d normally incur a penalty, even though he only had 13 clubs in his bag at the time. For what it’s worth, he did later get back the missing club. – John Jay, Conneaut Lake, PA

An interesting question, worthy of the original John Jay, who as you no doubt know was a Founding Father, the first Chief Justice of the United States, and the second governor of New York. But we digress.

Golf.title: Irish Open will feel 'different' with Trump visit
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy admits this year's Irish Open will feel like a "different" spectacle given US President Donald Trump's anticipated visit during the tournament.
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy admits this year's Irish Open will feel like a "different" spectacle given US President Donald Trump's anticipated visit during the tournament's latter stages. Trump is expected to attend the event - which is being held at his resort in the County Clare village of Doonbeg - this weekend as part of a two-day visit to Ireland.

McIlroy has previously played golf with Trump, who earlier this year praised the Northern Irishman's accomplishments on the course after winning back-to-back Masters titles. "It's going to be different, but the one thing I'd say is his golf resorts have hosted PGA Tour events, European Tour events, LIV events," McIlroy told BBC Sport NI's Stephen Watson.

Golf.title: ‘I still have a contract with LIV that I’m more than willing to fulfil’ — Jon Rahm on facing career uncertainty
Golf.summary: ‘I still have a contract with LIV that I’m more than willing to fulfil’ — Jon Rahm on facing career uncertainty Irish Independent
Golf.body:
If LIV’s Jon Rahm dances his way between the dunes and bunkers at Doonbeg as deftly as he dodges questions about his future, he has a third Irish Open title in the bag. Bobbing and weaving like Urtain — the Basque José Manuel Ibar Azpiazu who became EBU heavyweight champion in 1970 and 1971 — the two-time Irish Open winner would not be pinned on the ropes about his future with the breakaway circuit.

Amid reports from the Financial Times that LIV Golf is looking to file for bankruptcy protection in the wake of Saudi Arabia’s PIF pulling its funding, leaving CEO Scott O’Neil scrambling to find backers to LIV Golf 2.0, the Spanish star was giving little away as wind and rain, mixed with occasional sunny spells, kept the players on their toes in west Clare.

Golf.title: As Cabot Revelstoke nears completion, excitement comes with the territory
Golf.summary: Sometimes the pursuit of exquisite golf means crossing oceans, although for Cabot Revelstoke it’s just a border away. The post As Cabot Revelstoke nears completion, excitement comes with the territory appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Rod Whitman has spent more than four decades building great golf courses and almost no time building the Rod Whitman brand. At 72, the Canadian-born course designer has quietly assembled one of the game’s most respected résumés. After apprenticing under Pete Dye and shaping for Bill Coore and Ben Crenshaw, Whitman struck out on his own in 1984, going on to solo-design Cabot Links and shape acclaimed courses like Friars Head and Old Sandwich. His work has drawn a spotlight that Whitman hasn’t clamored for himself. He doesn’t have a computer or a publicist. He isn’t on social media.

“I feel like the past 40 years, I’ve mostly just been working,” he says on a recent morning from the tee of a short, downhill par 3. It was just past dawn, the sun peaking over the mountains of British Columbia, and Whitman was busy with his latest job, putting the finishing touches on Cabot Revelstoke, his own design and the centerpiece of Cabot’s plans for a new alpine destination.

Golf.title: PGA Tour denied request for LIV Golf stars to be picked for Presidents Cup
Golf.summary: PGA Tour denied request for LIV Golf stars to be picked for Presidents Cup AOL.com
Golf.body:
The PGA Tour has denied a request for international LIV Golf stars to compete in this year's Presidents Cup, shunning the likes of Cameron Smith and Lucas Herbert for the competition at Medinah later this month. International team captain Geoff Ogilvy had hoped to bolster his roster ahead of the Presidents Cup, with the team was significantly depleted since the start of LIV Golf.

It will be the third Presidents Cup since LIV Golf arrived on the scene, and the split has had a major impact on the International team. Half of the side that played at Royal Melbourne in 2019 have since moved to LIV, leaving the competition without some of the players who helped make up the International team's strongest recent line-ups.

Golf.title: For the second-generation ZXi irons, Srixon turned to a legendary partner
Golf.summary: Srixon's second-generation ZXi irons improve on the popular line with a new partnership with one of the game's legendary forging houses. The post For the second-generation ZXi irons, Srixon turned to a legendary partner appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When it comes to forged irons, the name Endo Manufacturing can stop gearheads in their tracks. Srixon is counting on it with their second-generation ZXi irons. In releasing the updated line, which again includes the ZXi7, ZXi5 and ZXiU irons, along with the new ZXi5+ players distance iron, Srixon is announcing that all four irons are forged by the legendary Japanese forging house.

“We’ve been working with Endo for a long time,” Srixon Senior Product Manager Casey Schultz told GOLF. “We’ve had a relationship with them in the past, but this is the first time that we’ve been able to really kind of announce the fact that every single iron is being made there.”

Golf.title: The September golf schedule? It's for the diehards
Golf.summary: The Tour Championship is over and football season is right around the corner, but some of the best golf of the year is right in front of us. The post The September golf schedule? It’s for the diehards appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
There’s a common misconception that the golf season ends in August. Next up: the California Swing, five months out. Or, for the real casuals, the Masters, eight months away. But that’s far from reality. Your uncle Mark probably knows about the Memorial and U.S. Open and Pebble Beach and that crazy 16th hole at TPC Scottsdale, but it’s the true diehard, sicko golf fans who get excited for all the wonderful September golf ahead and things like Lahinch (last week’s Walker Cup venue), an Irish Open (names like Rahm, McIlroy and Koepka are playing) and Wentworth (host of the BMW Championship, the DP World Tour’s flagship event).

September is an intoxicating mix of team events and tournaments contested on old layouts that us lucky Americans get to watch in the mornings. That’s the best kind of golf, the golf you can watch when you wake up, when fall is approaching and it’s starting to get chilly in the States but not quite as cold as what it looks like on TV at Doughmore Beach, a few steps from where they’re playing the Irish Open at Trump International Golf Links & Hotel. (The coffee, with the smallest splash of cream, always tastes better too.)

Golf.title: This no-fuss training aid solves a common swing issue
Golf.summary: Since its inception in 2014, the Smart Ball remains wildly popular, and the Smart Ball Sleeve lets you attach it anywhere. The post This no-fuss training aid solves a common swing issue appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When GOLF’s own Top 100 Teacher Martin Chuck created the Smart Ball, his goal was simple: Make a no-fuss training aid that actually solves a common swing issue. Just put the lanyard around your neck and the Smart Ball helps you keep your arms connected and your body rotating properly.
